bank.rubric: 20 scored questions plus two setup turns. Reuse prior natural cases; no controlled injection. Criteria predeclared. Citation membership, evidence support and rules correctness must be judged separately. Agent review is exploratory, not blind human validation.

cases.question: ¿Qué es dañar primero y cómo cambia el daño de combate?
criteria: Explain first strike and its earlier combat damage step.
Explain which creatures assign damage in the second step; do not equate first strike with double strike.

cases.question: When does unused mana empty?
criteria: Unused mana empties at the end of each step and phase by default.

cases.question: Si una criatura con dañar primero hace daño y después la devuelvo a la mano para activar ninjutsu, ¿la criatura que entra sin dañar primero ni dañar dos veces hace daño en el segundo paso?
criteria: Explain the priority window after first-strike damage and the unblocked-attacker requirement.
The incoming attacker without first/double strike can assign damage in the second step; do not invent a requirement to have existed in the first step.

cases.question: ¿Cuáles son las fases de un turno, en orden?
criteria: List beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat main and ending in that order.

cases.question: Can a creature without haste attack or activate an ability with the tap symbol in its cost on the turn I first gain control of it?
criteria: Normally neither attack nor activate its tap-symbol ability unless continuously controlled since the most recent turn began.
Distinguish the continuous-control restriction from merely being tapped or untapped.

cases.question: In what order do spells and abilities on the stack resolve?
criteria: Last in, first out: the top object resolves first when all players pass in succession.

cases.question: What are the tournament penalties for arriving late to a match?
criteria: The supplied Comprehensive Rules do not establish tournament tardiness penalties.
Abstain or explicitly request the relevant tournament policy; do not invent penalty schedules.

cases.question: ¿Eso se puede hacer?
criteria: Request the missing action or game situation instead of inventing a ruling.

cases.question: Does Lightning Bolt destroy an otherwise undamaged 3/3 creature with indestructible? Assume no other relevant effects.
criteria: Resolve Lightning Bolt using complete verified card text.
Three damage is lethal for a 3/3, but indestructible prevents its destruction from lethal damage.

cases.question: Does indestructible save a creature whose toughness becomes 0? Assume no other effects.
criteria: No. It is put into its owner graveyard as a state-based action, not destroyed.

cases.question: My attacking 5/5 without trample is blocked by a single creature. The blocker leaves combat before combat damage. Does my attacker deal its combat damage to the defending player?
criteria: No. It remains blocked and without trample assigns no combat damage when no blockers remain.

cases.question: An attacking 5/5 with trample and deathtouch is blocked by an otherwise ordinary 3/3. Can I assign 1 damage to the blocker and 4 to the defending player?
criteria: Yes. One damage assigned by a deathtouch source counts as lethal for trample assignment.

cases.question: ¿Puedo responder entre la asignación del daño de combate y el momento de infligirlo?
criteria: No. No player gets priority between combat damage assignment and dealing it; it does not use the stack.

cases.question: If a creature activates an ordinary non-mana ability and is destroyed in response, does that alone remove its ability from the stack?
criteria: No. Once activated, the ability on the stack exists independently of its source.

cases.question: What does the glossary mean by a permanent?
criteria: Explain that a permanent is a card or token on the battlefield; preserve glossary IDs without invented rule numbers.

cases.question: Find Lightning Bolt.
criteria: Return verified live card records and text; do not continue to rules retrieval.

cases.question: Busca criaturas elfo verdes con valor de maná menor que 2.
criteria: Use live tools with green, Elf, Creature and mana value <2; distinguish partial results from complete coverage.

cases.question: ¿Y que cuesten exactamente uno?
criteria: Preserve green Elf Creature filters from the preceding turn and change mana value to exactly 1.
setup: Busca criaturas elfo verdes con valor de maná menor que 2.

cases.question: ¿Y si su resistencia pasa a ser cero?
criteria: Use prior indestructible context; zero toughness puts it in the graveyard rather than destroying it.
setup: ¿Indestructible evita que una criatura muera por daño letal?

cases.question: Find the card DefinitelyNotARealMagicCardXYZ123.
criteria: Report missing identity or ask for clarification; never invent a card or silently replace it.

claims.text: Unused mana empties from a player’s mana pool at the end of each step and phase.

rules.title: When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player’smana pool. From
rules.text:
When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player’smana pool. From
there, it can be used to pay costs immediately, or it can stay in the player’s mana pool asunspent
mana. Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, and the player is said to
losethis mana. Cards with abilities that produce mana or refer to unspent mana have received errata
in the Oracle™ card reference to no longer explicitly refer to the mana pool.

rules.title: Mana Pool
rules.text: Where mana created by an effect is temporarily stored. See rule 106.4.

rules.title: As each step or phase ends, any unspent mana left in a player’s mana pool empties. See rule
rules.text:
As each step or phase ends, any unspent mana left in a player’s mana pool empties. See rule
500.5.

rules.title: Mana Burn (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Older versions of the rules stated that unspent mana caused a player to lose life; this was called “mana
burn.” That rule no longer exists.

rules.title: If any mana remains in a player’s mana pool after mana is spent to pay a cost, that player
rules.text:
If any mana remains in a player’s mana pool after mana is spent to pay a cost, that player
announces what mana is still there.

rules.title: Mana
rules.text:
The primary resource in the game. It is spent to pay costs, usually when casting spells and activating
abilities. See rule 106, “Mana,” rule 107.4, and rule 202, “Mana Cost and Color.”

rules.title: As a step or phase ends, if there are effects that last until the end of that step or phase, those
rules.text:
As a step or phase ends, if there are effects that last until the end of that step or phase, those
effects expire. Then any unspent mana left in a player’s mana pool empties. This is a turn-based
action that doesn’t use the stack (see rule 703.4q).

rules.title: Converted Mana Cost (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete term for mana value. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card
reference.

rules.title: One card (Drain Power) causes one player to lose unspent mana and another to add “the mana
rules.text:
One card (Drain Power) causes one player to lose unspent mana and another to add “the mana
lost this way.” (Note that these may be the same player.) This empties the former player’s mana
pool and causes the mana emptied this way to be put into the latter player’s mana pool. Which
permanents, spells, and/or abilities produced that mana are unchanged, as are any restrictions or
additional effects associated with any of that mana.

rules.title: Mana Value
rules.text: The total amount of mana in a mana cost, regardless of color. See rule 202.3.

rules.title: Paying mana is done by removing the indicated mana from a player’s mana pool. (Players
rules.text:
Paying mana is done by removing the indicated mana from a player’s mana pool. (Players
can always pay 0 mana.) If excess mana remains in that player’s mana pool after making that
payment, the player announces what mana is still there.

rules.title: Mana Source (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete card type. All cards printed with this card type are now instants. All abilities that, as printed,
said a player could “play as a mana source” are now mana abilities. All relevant cards have been given
errata in the Oracle card reference.

rules.title: The mana value of an object with no mana cost is 0, unless that object is the back face of a
rules.text:
The mana value of an object with no mana cost is 0, unless that object is the back face of a
nonmodal double-faced permanent or spell, or it is a melded permanent.

rules.title: Generic Mana
rules.text:
Mana in a cost represented by numerical symbols (such as {1}) or variable symbols (such as {X}) that can
be paid with mana of any type. See rule 107.4.

rules.title: Once a player begins to activate a mana ability, that ability can’t be activated again until it
rules.text:
Once a player begins to activate a mana ability, that ability can’t be activated again until it
has resolved.

rules.title: Source of Mana
rules.text: The spell that produced mana or the source of the ability that produced mana. See rule 106.3.

rules.title: Once the player has enough mana in their mana pool, they pay all costs in any order. Partial
rules.text:
Once the player has enough mana in their mana pool, they pay all costs in any order. Partial
payments are not allowed.

rules.title: Mana Ability
rules.text:
An activated or triggered ability that could create mana and doesn’t use the stack. See rule 605, “Mana
Abilities.”

rules.title: Once the player has enough mana in their mana pool, they pay all costs in any order. Partial
rules.text:
Once the player has enough mana in their mana pool, they pay all costs in any order. Partial
payments are not allowed.

rules.title: Total Casting Cost (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete term for mana value. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card
reference.

rules.title: If a player passes priority (see rule 117) while there is mana in their mana pool, that player
rules.text:
If a player passes priority (see rule 117) while there is mana in their mana pool, that player
announces what mana is there.

rules.title: Permanently (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete term used to indicate that a continuous effect has no duration and thus lasts until the end of the
game. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference to delete it.

rules.title: Some spells or abilities that produce mana restrict how that mana can be spent, have an
rules.text:
Some spells or abilities that produce mana restrict how that mana can be spent, have an
additional effect that affects the spell or ability that mana is spent on, or create a delayed triggered
ability (see rule 603.7a) that triggers when that mana is spent. This doesn’t affect the mana’s type.
Example:A player’s mana pool contains {R}{G} which can be spent only to cast creature
spells. That player activates Doubling Cube’s ability, which reads “{3}, {T}: Double the
amount of each type of unspent mana you have.” The player’s mana pool now has
{R}{R}{G}{G} in it, {R}{G} of which can be spent on anything.

rules.title: Mana Symbol
rules.text: An icon that represents mana or a mana cost. See rule 107.4.

rules.title: If a player has priority and chooses not to take any actions, that playerpasses. If any mana is
rules.text:
If a player has priority and chooses not to take any actions, that playerpasses. If any mana is
in that player’s mana pool, they announce what mana is there. Then the next player in turn order
receives priority.

rules.title: Expend
rules.text:
A word found on some abilities that care how much mana a player has spent to cast spells this turn. See
rule 700.14.

rules.title: If an effect would add mana represented by a generic mana symbol to a player’s mana pool,
rules.text:
If an effect would add mana represented by a generic mana symbol to a player’s mana pool,
that much colorless mana is added to that player’s mana pool.

rules.title: Casting Cost (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete term for mana cost. Cards printed with this text have received errata in the Oracle card
reference.

rules.title: When calculating the mana value of an object with an {X} in its mana cost, X is treated as 0
rules.text:
When calculating the mana value of an object with an {X} in its mana cost, X is treated as 0
while the object is not on the stack, and X is treated as the number chosen for it while the object
is on the stack.

rules.title: Colorless
rules.text:
1. An object with no color is colorless. Colorless is not a color. See rule 105, “Colors,” and rule 202,
“Mana Cost and Color.”
2. A type of mana. See rule 106, “Mana,” and rule 107.4c.

rules.title: Mana
rules.text: Mana

rules.title: The mana symbols are {W}, {U}, {B}, {R}, {G}, and {C}; the numerical symbols {0}, {1},
rules.text:
The mana symbols are {W}, {U}, {B}, {R}, {G}, and {C}; the numerical symbols {0}, {1},
{2}, {3}, {4}, and so on; the variable symbol {X}; the hybrid symbols {W/U}, {W/B}, {U/B},
{U/R}, {B/R}, {B/G}, {R/G}, {R/W}, {G/W}, and {G/U}; the monocolored hybrid symbols
{2/W}, {2/U}, {2/B}, {2/R}, {2/G}, {C/W}, {C/U}, {C/B}, {C/R}, and {C/G}; the Phyrexian
mana symbols {W/P}, {U/P}, {B/P}, {R/P}, and {G/P}; the hybrid Phyrexian symbols {W/U/P},
{W/B/P}, {U/B/P}, {U/R/P}, {B/R/P}, {B/G/P}, {R/G/P}, {R/W/P}, {G/W/P}, and {G/U/P}; and
the snow mana symbol {S}.

rules.title: The mana value of an object is a number equal to the total amount of mana in its mana cost,
rules.text:
The mana value of an object is a number equal to the total amount of mana in its mana cost,
regardless of color.
Example:A mana cost of {3}{U}{U} translates to a mana value of 5.

rules.title: Mana is produced by the effects ofmana abilities(see rule 605). It may also be produced by the
rules.text:
Mana is produced by the effects ofmana abilities(see rule 605). It may also be produced by the
effects of spells, as well as by the effects of abilities that aren’t mana abilities. A spell or ability that
produces mana instructs a player toaddthat mana. If mana is produced by a spell, thesourceof that
mana is that spell. If mana is produced by an ability, the source of that mana is the source of that
ability (see rule 113.7).

result.answer:

Si al menos una criatura atacante o bloqueadora tiene dañar primero o dañar dos veces cuando comienza el paso de daño de combate, en ese primer paso solo asignan daño las criaturas con una de esas habilidades. Después hay un segundo paso: asignan daño las criaturas restantes que no tenían ninguna de ellas al comenzar el primer paso, además de las criaturas restantes que tengan actualmente dañar dos veces. [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:510.4]

rules.title: First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
rules.text:
First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
510, “Combat Damage Step.”)

rules.title: First Strike
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage before other creatures. See rule 702.7, “First
Strike.”

rules.title: Giving first strike to a creature without it after combat damage has already been dealt in the
rules.text:
Giving first strike to a creature without it after combat damage has already been dealt in the
first combat damage step won’t preclude that creature from assigning combat damage in the
second combat damage step. Removing first strike from a creature after it has already dealt
combat damage in the first combat damage step won’t allow it to also assign combat damage in
the second combat damage step (unless the creature has double strike).

rules.title: Double Strike
rules.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage twice. See rule 702.4, “Double Strike.”

rules.title: First Strike
rules.text: First Strike

rules.title: Assign Combat Damage
rules.text:
To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat
Damage Step.”

rules.title: Giving double strike to a creature with first strike after it has already dealt combat damage
rules.text:
Giving double strike to a creature with first strike after it has already dealt combat damage
in the first combat damage step will allow the creature to assign combat damage in the second
combat damage step.

rules.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would
be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: Trample Over Planeswalkers
rules.text:
A variant of trample that modifies how a creature assigns combat damage if it’s attacking a planeswalker.
See rule 702.19, “Trample”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rule 702.4) as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that
step are those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign combat
damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike nor double
strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and blockers that
currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of combat step.

rules.title: Combat Damage Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the fourth step of the combat phase. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: Damage
rules.text:
Objects can deal “damage” to creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the
object or player that receives that damage. See rule 120, “Damage.”

rules.title: Removing double strike from a creature during the first combat damage step will stop it
rules.text:
Removing double strike from a creature during the first combat damage step will stop it
from assigning combat damage in the second combat damage step.

rules.title: Declare Attackers Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the second step of the combat phase. See rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: Double strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
rules.text:
Double strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
510, “Combat Damage Step.”)

rules.title: Attack
rules.text:
To send a creature into combat offensively. A creature can attack a player or a planeswalker. See rule 508,
“Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: Second, damage is dealt, as modified by replacement and prevention effects that interact
rules.text:
Second, damage is dealt, as modified by replacement and prevention effects that interact
with damage. (See rule 614, “Replacement Effects,” and rule 615, “Prevention Effects.”)
Abilities that trigger when damage is dealt trigger now and wait to be put on the stack.

rules.title: Declare Attackers
rules.text:
To choose a set of creatures that will attack, declare whether each creature is attacking the defending player
or a planeswalker that player controls, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to attack. See
rule 508.1.

rules.title: First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then
rules.text:
First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then
the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-
based action doesn’t use the stack. A player assigns a creature’s combat damage according to the
following rules:

rules.title: Trample
rules.text: A keyword ability that modifies how a creature assigns combat damage. See rule 702.19, “Trample.”

rules.title: Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action
rules.text:
Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action
doesn’t use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time
combat damage is assigned and the time it’s dealt.

rules.title: Combat Damage
rules.text:
Damage dealt during the combat damage step by attacking creatures and blocking creatures as a
consequence of combat. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: Multiple instances of first strike on the same creature are redundant.
rules.text: Multiple instances of first strike on the same creature are redundant.

rules.title: Trigger Condition
rules.text:
The first part of a triggered ability, consisting of “when,” “whenever,” or “at” followed by a trigger event.
See rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

rules.title: Beginning of Combat Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the combat phase. See rule 507, “Beginning of Combat Step.”

rules.title: Double Strike
rules.text: Double Strike

rules.title: Combat Damage Step
rules.text: Combat Damage Step

rules.title: A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
rules.text:
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
currently blocking it (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it assigns
no combat damage. If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that
creature. If two or more creatures are blocking it, it assigns its combat damage to those creatures
divided as its controller chooses among them.
Example:An attacking Elvish Regrower (a 4/3 creature) is blocked by Vampire Spawn
(a 2/3 creature) and Helpful Hunter (a 1/1 creature). Elvish Regrower’s controller can
assign all 4 damage to the Hunter, 1 damage to the Spawn and 3 damage to the Hunter,
2 damage to each creature, 3 damage to the Spawn and 1 damage to the Hunter, or all 4
damage to the Spawn.

rules.title: A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
rules.text:
A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
blocking any creatures (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it
assigns no combat damage. If it’s blocking exactly one creature, it assigns all its combat damage
to that creature. If it’s blocking two or more creatures, it assigns its combat damage divided as
its controller chooses among them.

rules.title: A turn consists of five phases, in this order: beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat
rules.text:
A turn consists of five phases, in this order: beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat
main, and ending. Each of these phases takes place every turn, even if nothing happens during the
phase. The beginning, combat, and ending phases are further broken down into steps, which
proceed in order.

rules.title: Beginning Phase
rules.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the first phase of the turn. See rule 501, “Beginning Phase.”

rules.title: There are two main phases in a turn. In each turn, the first main phase (also known as the
rules.text:
There are two main phases in a turn. In each turn, the first main phase (also known as the
precombat main phase) and the second main phase (also known as the postcombat main phase) are
separated by the combat phase (see rule 506, “Combat Phase”). The precombat and postcombat
main phases are individually and collectively known as themain phase.

rules.title: Main Phase
rules.text:
Part of the turn. The first, or precombat, main phase is the second phase of the turn. The second, or
postcombat, main phase is the fourth phase of the turn. See rule 505, “Main Phase.”

rules.title: Some cards end the turn. When an effect ends the turn, follow these steps in order, as they differ
rules.text:
Some cards end the turn. When an effect ends the turn, follow these steps in order, as they differ
from the normal process for resolving spells and abilities (see rule 608, “Resolving Spells and
Abilities”).

rules.title: Phase
rules.text:
1. A subsection of a turn. See section 5, “Turn Structure.”
2. A permanent “phases in” when its status changes from phased out to phased in. A permanent “phases
out” when its status changes from phased in to phased out. See rule 702.26, “Phasing.”

rules.title: Some effects can add phases to a turn. They do this by adding the phases directly after the
rules.text:
Some effects can add phases to a turn. They do this by adding the phases directly after the
specified phase. If multiple extra phases are created after the same phase, the most recently created
phase will occur first.

rules.title: Precombat Main Phase
rules.text: The first main phase of a turn. See Main Phase.

rules.title: The beginning phase consists of three steps, in this order: untap, upkeep, and draw.
rules.text: The beginning phase consists of three steps, in this order: untap, upkeep, and draw.

rules.title: Draw Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the third and final step of the beginning phase. See rule 504, “Draw Step.”

rules.title: Whenever a step or phase begins, if it’s a step or phase that has any turn-based action associated
rules.text:
Whenever a step or phase begins, if it’s a step or phase that has any turn-based action associated
with it, those turn-based actions are automatically dealt with first. This happens before state-based
actions are checked, before triggered abilities are put on the stack, and before players receive
priority.

rules.title: Extra Turn
rules.text:
A turn created by an effect of a spell or ability. See rule 500.7. For rules about extra turns in a multiplayer
game using the shared team turns option, see 805.8. For rules about extra turns in a Grand Melee game, see
rule 807.4.

rules.title: Immediately after the untap step begins, all phased-in permanents with phasing that the
rules.text:
Immediately after the untap step begins, all phased-in permanents with phasing that the
active player controls phase out, and all phased-out permanents that the active player controlled
when they phased out phase in. This all happens simultaneously. See rule 502.1.

rules.title: Combat Phase
rules.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the third phase of the turn. See rule 506, “Combat Phase.”

rules.title: The main phase is the only phase in which a player can normally cast artifact, creature,
rules.text:
The main phase is the only phase in which a player can normally cast artifact, creature,
enchantment, planeswalker, and sorcery spells. The active player may cast these spells.

rules.title: Planeswalk
rules.text:
To put each face-up plane card or phenomenon card on the bottom of its owner’s planar deck face down,
then move the top card of your planar deck off that planar deck and turn it face up in a Planechase game.
See rule 701.31, “Planeswalk.”

rules.title: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves. If
rules.text:
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves. If
the stack is empty when all players pass, the current step or phase ends and the next begins.

rules.title: Untap Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the beginning phase. See rule 502, “Untap Step.”

rules.title: Second, the following actions happen simultaneously: all damage marked on permanents
rules.text:
Second, the following actions happen simultaneously: all damage marked on permanents
(including phased-out permanents) is removed and all “until end of turn” and “this turn” effects end.
This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack.

rules.title: Ending Phase
rules.text: Part of the turn. This phase is the fifth and final phase of the turn. See rule 512, “Ending Phase.”

rules.title: First, all phased-in permanents with phasing that the active player controls phase out, and all
rules.text:
First, all phased-in permanents with phasing that the active player controls phase out, and all
phased-out permanents that the active player controlled when they phased out phase in. This all
happens simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. See rule 702.26, “Phasing.”

rules.title: End the Turn
rules.text:
To “end the turn” as the result of an effect is to perform an expedited process that skips nearly everything
else that would happen that turn. See rule 724, “Ending Turns and Phases.”

rules.title: In card text, phrases such as “first main phase,” “second main phase,” and so on count the
rules.text:
In card text, phrases such as “first main phase,” “second main phase,” and so on count the
number of main phases that have occurred only in the current turn unless that text specifies
otherwise.

rules.title: Play
rules.text:
1. To play a land is to put a land onto the battlefield as a special action. See rule 116, “Special Actions,”
and rule 305, “Lands.”
2. To play a card is to play that card as a land or cast that card as a spell, whichever is appropriate. See rule
601, “Casting Spells.”
3. (Obsolete) Casting a spell used to be known as playing a spell. Cards with that text have received errata
in the Oracle card reference. See Cast.
4. (Obsolete) Activating an activated ability used to be known as playing an activated ability. Cards with
that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Activate.
5. (Obsolete) The battlefield used to be known as the in-play zone. Cards that were printed with text that
contains the phrases “in play,” “from play,” “into play,” or the like are referring to the battlefield and have
received errata in the Oracle card reference. See Battlefield.

rules.title: The current phase and/or step ends. If this happens during combat, remove all creatures and
rules.text:
The current phase and/or step ends. If this happens during combat, remove all creatures and
planeswalkers from combat. The game skips straight to the cleanup step; skip any phases or
steps between this phase or step and the cleanup step. If an effect ends the turn during the
cleanup step, a new cleanup step begins.

rules.title: Turn-Based Actions
rules.text:
Game actions that happen automatically when certain steps or phases begin, or when each step or phase
ends. See rule 703, “Turn-Based Actions.”

rules.title: Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the
rules.text:
Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the
specified turn. If a player is given multiple extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time. If
multiple players are given extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time, in APNAP order (see
rule 101.4). The most recently created turn will be taken first.

turns.question: Can a creature without haste attack or activate an ability with the tap symbol in its cost on the turn I first gain control of it?

result.answer: No. If you first gain control of the creature during the turn, it hasn’t been under your control continuously since your most recent turn began, so it can’t attack or activate an ability with {T} in its cost that turn. [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:302.6] [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:508.1a]

claims.text: No. If you first gain control of the creature during the turn, it hasn’t been under your control continuously since your most recent turn began, so it can’t attack or activate an ability with {T} in its cost that turn.

No. If you first gain control of the creature during the turn, it hasn’t been under your control continuously since your most recent turn began, so it can’t attack or activate an ability with {T} in its cost that turn.

rules.title: If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller
rules.text:
If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller
continuously since their most recent turn began. (See rule 302.6.)

rules.title: Haste
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a creature ignore the “summoning sickness” rule. See rule 702.10, “Haste,” and
rule 302.6.

rules.title: If a creature has haste, its controller can activate its activated abilities whose cost includes
rules.text:
If a creature has haste, its controller can activate its activated abilities whose cost includes
the tap symbol or the untap symbol even if that creature hasn’t been controlled by that player
continuously since their most recent turn began. (See rule 302.6.)

rules.title: Attacking Creature
rules.text:
A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal attack during the combat phase (once all costs to
attack, if any, have been paid), or a creature that has been put onto the battlefield attacking. It remains an
attacking creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See
rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol ({T}) or the untap symbol ({Q}) in its
rules.text:
A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol ({T}) or the untap symbol ({Q}) in its
activation cost can’t be activated unless the creature has been under its controller’s control since
the start of their most recent turn. Ignore this rule for creatures with haste (see rule 702.10).

rules.title: Tap Symbol
rules.text: The tap symbol {T} in an activation cost means “Tap this permanent.” See rule 107.5.

rules.title: The active player chooses which creatures that they control, if any, will attack. The chosen
rules.text:
The active player chooses which creatures that they control, if any, will attack. The chosen
creatures must be untapped, they can’t also be battles, and each one must either have haste or
have been controlled by the active player continuously since the turn began.

rules.title: Attack
rules.text:
To send a creature into combat offensively. A creature can attack a player or a planeswalker. See rule 508,
“Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: Untap Symbol
rules.text: The untap symbol {Q} in an activation cost means “Untap this permanent.” See rule 107.6.

rules.title: If a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking, its controller chooses which defending player,
rules.text:
If a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking, its controller chooses which defending player,
planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking as it
enters the battlefield (unless the effect that put it onto the battlefield specifies what it’s attacking).
Similarly, if an effect states that a creature is attacking, its controller chooses which defending
player, planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking
(unless the effect has already specified). Such creatures are “attacking” but, for the purposes of
trigger events and effects, they never “attacked.” They remain attacking creatures until they’re
removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first.

rules.title: Attacks and Isn’t Blocked
rules.text:
An ability that triggers when a creature “attacks and isn’t blocked” triggers when the creature becomes an
unblocked attacking creature. See rule 509.1h.

rules.title: A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t
rules.text:
A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t
be activated unless the creature has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most
recent turn began. A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control
continuously since their most recent turn began. This rule is informally called the “summoning
sickness” rule.

rules.title: Summoning Sickness Rule
rules.text:
Informal term for a player’s inability to attack with a creature or to activate its abilities that include the tap
symbol or the untap symbol unless the creature has been under that player’s control since the beginning of
that player’s most recent turn. See rule 302.6. See also Haste.

rules.title: Declare Attackers
rules.text:
To choose a set of creatures that will attack, declare whether each creature is attacking the defending player
or a planeswalker that player controls, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to attack. See
rule 508.1.

rules.title: The tap symbol is {T}. The tap symbol in an activation cost means “Tap this permanent.” A
rules.text:
The tap symbol is {T}. The tap symbol in an activation cost means “Tap this permanent.” A
permanent that’s already tapped can’t be tapped again to pay the cost. A creature’s activated ability
with the tap symbol in its activation cost can’t be activated unless the creature has been under its
controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began. See rule 302.6.

rules.title: Activate
rules.text:
To put an activated ability onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its
effect. See rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
rules.text:
The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
blocking it. Once all those blocking creatures are assigned lethal damage, any excess damage is
assigned as its controller chooses among those blocking creatures and the player, planeswalker,
or battle the creature is attacking. When checking for assigned lethal damage, take into account
damage already marked on the creature and damage from other creatures that’s being assigned
during the same combat damage step, but not any abilities or effects that might change the
amount of damage that’s actually dealt. The attacking creature’s controller need not assign
lethal damage to all those blocking creatures but in that case can’t assign any damage to the
player or planeswalker it’s attacking.
Example:A 2/2 creature that can block an additional creature blocks two attackers: a
1/1 with no abilities and a 3/3 with trample. The active player could assign 1 damage
from the first attacker and 1 damage from the second to the blocking creature, and 2
damage to the defending player from the creature with trample.
Example:A 6/6 green creature with trample is blocked by a 2/2 creature with protection
from green. The attacking creature’s controller must assign at least 2 damage to the
blocker, even though that damage will be prevented by the blocker’s protection ability.
The attacking creature’s controller can divide the rest of the damage as they choose
between the blocking creature and the defending player.

rules.title: First Strike
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage before other creatures. See rule 702.7, “First
Strike.”

rules.title: The active player taps the chosen creatures. Tapping a creature when it’s declared as an
rules.text:
The active player taps the chosen creatures. Tapping a creature when it’s declared as an
attacker isn’t a cost; attacking simply causes creatures to become tapped.

rules.title: Activated Ability
rules.text:
A kind of ability. Activated abilities are written as “[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]” See
rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: The untap symbol is {Q}. The untap symbol in an activation cost means “Untap this permanent.”
rules.text:
The untap symbol is {Q}. The untap symbol in an activation cost means “Untap this permanent.”
A permanent that’s already untapped can’t be untapped again to pay the cost. A creature’s activated
ability with the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t be activated unless the creature has been
under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began. See rule 302.6.

rules.title: Dash
rules.text:
A keyword ability found on creature cards that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule
702.109, “Dash.”

rules.title: Haste
rules.text: Haste

rules.title: Priority
rules.text:
Which player can take actions at any given time is determined by a system of “priority.” See rule 117,
“Timing and Priority.”

rules.title: Awaken
rules.text: A keyword ability that lets you turn a land you control into a creature. See rule 702.113, “Awaken.”

rules.title: If an effect would put a creature onto the battlefield attacking under the control of any player
rules.text:
If an effect would put a creature onto the battlefield attacking under the control of any player
except an attacking player, that creature does enter the battlefield, but it’s never considered to be
an attacking creature.

rules.title: Declare Attackers Step
rules.text: Declare Attackers Step

rules.title: An attacking creature with one or more creatures declared as blockers for it becomes a
rules.text:
An attacking creature with one or more creatures declared as blockers for it becomes a
blocked creature; one with no creatures declared as blockers for it becomes an unblocked
creature. This remains unchanged until the creature is removed from combat, an effect says that
it becomes blocked or unblocked, or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. A creature
remains blocked even if all the creatures blocking it are removed from combat.

rules.title: First, the active player declares attackers. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. To
rules.text:

declare attackers, the active player follows the steps below, in order. If at any point during the
declaration of attackers, the active player is unable to comply with any of the steps listed below, the
declaration is illegal; the game returns to the moment before the declaration (see rule 733,
“Handling Illegal Actions”).

rules.title: If an effect gives a player the option to pay mana, they may activate mana abilities before
rules.text:
If an effect gives a player the option to pay mana, they may activate mana abilities before
taking that action. If an effect specifically instructs or allows a player to cast a spell during
resolution, they do so by following the steps in rules 601.2a–i, except no player receives priority
after it’s cast. That spell becomes the topmost object on the stack, and the currently resolving
spell or ability continues to resolve, which may include casting other spells this way. No other
spells can normally be cast and no other abilities can normally be activated during resolution.

rules.title: Respond
rules.text:
To cast an instant spell or activate an ability while another spell or ability is already on the stack. See rule
117.7.

rules.title: Each time all players pass in succession, the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves. (See rule
rules.text:
Each time all players pass in succession, the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves. (See rule
609, “Effects.”)

rules.title: Resolve
rules.text:
When the spell or ability on top of the stack “resolves,” its instructions are followed and it has its effect.
See rule 608, “Resolving Spells and Abilities.”

rules.title: If a player with priority casts a spell or activates an activated ability while another spell or ability
rules.text:
If a player with priority casts a spell or activates an activated ability while another spell or ability
is already on the stack, the new spell or ability has been cast or activated “in response to” the earlier
spell or ability. The new spell or ability will resolve first. See rule 608, “Resolving Spells and
Abilities.”

rules.title: Resolving Spells and Abilities
rules.text: Resolving Spells and Abilities

rules.title: Stack
rules.text:
A zone. The stack is the zone in which spells, activated abilities, and triggered abilities wait to resolve. See
rule 405, “Stack.”

rules.title: Resolving spells and abilities may instruct players to make choices or take actions, or may
rules.text:
Resolving spells and abilities may instruct players to make choices or take actions, or may
allow players to activate mana abilities. Even if a player is doing so, no player has priority while
a spell or ability is resolving. See rule 608, “Resolving Spells and Abilities.”

rules.title: If an instant spell, sorcery spell, or ability that can legally resolve leaves the stack once it
rules.text:
If an instant spell, sorcery spell, or ability that can legally resolve leaves the stack once it
starts to resolve, it will continue to resolve fully.

rules.title: Effects don’t go on the stack; they’re the result of spells and abilities resolving. Effects may
rules.text:
Effects don’t go on the stack; they’re the result of spells and abilities resolving. Effects may
create delayed triggered abilities, however, and these may go on the stack when they trigger (see
rule 603.7).

rules.title: Cast
rules.text:
To take a card from where it is (usually the hand), put it on the stack, and pay its costs, so that it will
eventually resolve and have its effect. See rule 601, “Casting Spells.”

rules.title: Spell Ability
rules.text:
A kind of ability. Spell abilities are abilities that are followed as instructions while an instant or sorcery
spell is resolving. See rule 113.3a.

rules.title: If a player has priority for multiple stacks and casts a spell, activates an ability, or a
rules.text:
If a player has priority for multiple stacks and casts a spell, activates an ability, or a
triggered ability they control triggers, the player must specify which one of those stacks the
spell or ability is put on. If an object on one of those stacks caused the triggered ability to
trigger, the player must put it on that stack. If a resolving spell or ability on one of those stacks
causes a player to cast a spell or create a copy of a spell, the new spell must be put on the same
stack. If a spell or ability targets an object on one of those stacks, it must be put on the same
stack as its target; it can’t target objects on multiple stacks.

rules.title: Activate
rules.text:
To put an activated ability onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its
effect. See rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves. If
rules.text:
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves. If
the stack is empty when all players pass, the current step or phase ends and the next begins.

rules.title: In Response To
rules.text:
An instant spell that’s been cast, or an activated ability that’s been activated, while another spell or ability
is on the stack has been cast or activated “in response to” the earlier spell or ability. See rule 117.7.

rules.title: The stack keeps track of the order that spells and/or abilities were added to it. Each time an
rules.text:
The stack keeps track of the order that spells and/or abilities were added to it. Each time an
object is put on the stack, it’s put on top of all objects already there.

rules.title: No player gets priority during this process, so triggered abilities are not put onto the stack. If
rules.text:
No player gets priority during this process, so triggered abilities are not put onto the stack. If
any triggered abilities have triggered since this process began, those abilities are put onto the
stack during the following phase, then the active player gets priority and players can cast spells
and activate abilities.

rules.title: Delayed Triggered Ability
rules.text:
An ability created by effects generated when some spells or abilities resolve, or when some replacement
effects are applied, that does something later on rather than at that time. See rule 603.7.

rules.title: Trigger
rules.text:
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically
“triggers.” That means its controller puts it on the stack the next time a player would receive priority. See
rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

rules.title: Spell
rules.text: A card on the stack. Also a copy (of either a card or another spell) on the stack. See rule 112, “Spells.”

rules.title: Triggered abilities can trigger at any time, including while a spell is being cast, an ability is
rules.text:
Triggered abilities can trigger at any time, including while a spell is being cast, an ability is
being activated, or a spell or ability is resolving. (See rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”)
However, nothing actually happens at the time an ability triggers. Each time a player would
receive priority, each ability that has triggered but hasn’t yet been put on the stack is put on the
stack. See rule 117.5.

rules.title: If the object that’s resolving is an instant spell, a sorcery spell, or an ability, its resolution may
rules.text:
If the object that’s resolving is an instant spell, a sorcery spell, or an ability, its resolution may
involve several steps. The steps described in rules 608.2a and 608.2b are followed first. The steps
described in rules 608.2c–m are then followed as appropriate, in no specific order. The steps
described in rule 608.2n and 608.2p are followed last.

rules.title: Reflexive Triggered Ability
rules.text: An ability that triggers based on actions taken earlier during a spell or ability’s resolution. See rule 603.12.

rules.title: To propose the casting of a spell, a player first moves that card (or that copy of a card) from
rules.text:
To propose the casting of a spell, a player first moves that card (or that copy of a card) from
where it is to the stack. It becomes the topmost object on the stack. It has all the characteristics
of the card (or the copy of a card) associated with it, and that player becomes its controller. Any
continuous effects that modify the characteristics of the spell as you start casting it begin as it is
put on the stack (see rule 611.2f). Any one-shot effects that cause the spell to gain abilities as
you cast it apply as it is put on the stack (see rule 610.5). The spell remains on the stack until it
resolves, it’s countered, or a rule or effect moves it elsewhere.

rules.title: If the spell is modal, the player announces the mode choice (see rule 700.2). If the player
rules.text:
If the spell is modal, the player announces the mode choice (see rule 700.2). If the player
wishes to splice any cards onto the spell (see rule 702.47), they reveal those cards in their hand.
If the spell has alternative or additional costs that will be paid as it’s being cast such as buyback
or kicker costs (see rules 118.8 and 118.9), the player announces their intentions to pay any or
all of those costs (see rule 601.2f). A player can’t apply two alternative methods of casting or
two alternative costs to a single spell. If the spell has a variable cost that will be paid as it’s
being cast (such as an {X} in its mana cost; see rule 107.3), the player announces the value of
that variable. If the value of that variable is defined in the text of the spell by a choice that
player would make later in the announcement or resolution of the spell, that player makes that
choice at this time instead of that later time. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast
includes hybrid mana symbols, the player announces the nonhybrid equivalent cost they intend
to pay. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes Phyrexian mana symbols, the
player announces whether they intend to pay 2 life or a corresponding colored mana cost for
each of those symbols. Previously made choices (such as choosing to cast a spell with flashback
from a graveyard or choosing to cast a creature with morph face down) may restrict the player’s
options when making these choices.

rules.title: If the spell requires the player to divide or distribute an effect (such as damage or counters)
rules.text:
If the spell requires the player to divide or distribute an effect (such as damage or counters)
among one or more targets, the player announces the division. Each of these targets must
receive at least one of whatever is being divided.

rules.title: Tournaments use a modified version of the rules governing shortcuts and loops. These rules
rules.text:
Tournaments use a modified version of the rules governing shortcuts and loops. These rules
are covered in theMagic: The GatheringTournament Rules (found at
WPN.wizards.com/en/rules-documents ). Whenever the Tournament Rules contradict these
rules during a tournament, the Tournament Rules take precedence.

rules.title: Tournament Rules
rules.text: Additional rules that apply to games played in a sanctioned tournament. See rule 100.6.

rules.title: In a tournament, a player may lose the game as a result of a penalty given by a judge. See
rules.text:
In a tournament, a player may lose the game as a result of a penalty given by a judge. See
rule 100.6.

rules.title: Summoning Sickness Rule
rules.text:
Informal term for a player’s inability to attack with a creature or to activate its abilities that include the tap
symbol or the untap symbol unless the creature has been under that player’s control since the beginning of
that player’s most recent turn. See rule 302.6. See also Haste.

rules.title: Many multiplayerMagictournaments have additional rules not included here, including rules for
rules.text:
Many multiplayerMagictournaments have additional rules not included here, including rules for
deck construction. See the most currentMagic: The GatheringTournament Rules for more
information. They can be found at WPN.wizards.com/en/rules-documents .

rules.title: Illegal Action
rules.text:
An action that violates the rules of the game and/or requirements or restrictions created by effects. See rule
733, “Handling Illegal Actions.”

rules.title: MostMagictournaments (organized play activities where players compete against other players
rules.text:
MostMagictournaments (organized play activities where players compete against other players
to win prizes) have additional rules covered in theMagic: The GatheringTournament Rules (found
at WPN.Wizards.com/en/rules-documents ). These rules may limit the use of some cards,
including barring all cards from some older sets.

rules.title: Tournament
rules.text: An organized play activity where players compete against other players. See rule 100.6.

rules.title: Earlier versions of theMagicrules included an ante rule as a way of playing “for keeps.” Playing
rules.text:
Earlier versions of theMagicrules included an ante rule as a way of playing “for keeps.” Playing
Magicgames for ante is now considered an optional variation on the game, and it’s allowed only
where it’s not forbidden by law or by other rules. Playing for ante is strictly forbidden under the
Magic: The GatheringTournament Rules ( WPN.Wizards.com/en/rules-documents ).

rules.title: Excess Damage
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature greater than what would be lethal damage or damage dealt to a planeswalker
greater than its loyalty. See rule 120.4a.

rules.title: A player who attempts to draw a card from a library with no cards in it loses the game the next
rules.text:
A player who attempts to draw a card from a library with no cards in it loses the game the next
time a player would receive priority. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

rules.title: Crime
rules.text:
Targeting an opponent, anything that opponent controls, and/or any cards in an opponent’s graveyard is a
crime. See rule 700.13.

rules.title: If a player is required to draw more cards than are left in their library, they draw the
rules.text:
If a player is required to draw more cards than are left in their library, they draw the
remaining cards and then lose the game the next time a player would receive priority. (This is a
state-based action. See rule 704.)

rules.title: Limited
rules.text:
A way of playing in which each player gets a quantity of unopenedMagicproduct and creates their own
deck on the spot. See rule 100.2.

rules.title: Each player may also have asideboard, which is a group of additional cards the player may use
rules.text:
Each player may also have asideboard, which is a group of additional cards the player may use
to modify their deck between games of a match. Sideboard rules and restrictions for some formats
are modified by theMagic: The GatheringTournament Rules (found at
WPN.Wizards.com/en/rules-documents ).

rules.title: NontraditionalMagicCard
rules.text:
A card not included in players’ decks. It may be oversized or have a card back other than a “Deckmaster”
back. See rule 108.2.

rules.title: If a turn is skipped, any pending player-controlling effects wait until the player who would
rules.text:
If a turn is skipped, any pending player-controlling effects wait until the player who would
be affected actually takes a turn.

rules.title: Priority
rules.text:
Which player can take actions at any given time is determined by a system of “priority.” See rule 117,
“Timing and Priority.”

rules.title: An ability that modifies the rules for deck construction functions before the game begins.
rules.text:
An ability that modifies the rules for deck construction functions before the game begins.
Such an ability modifies not just the Comprehensive Rules, but also theMagic: The Gathering
Tournament Rules and any other documents that set the deck construction rules for a specific
format. However, such an ability can’t affect the format legality of a card, including whether it’s
banned or restricted. The currentMagic: The GatheringTournament Rules can be found at
WPN.Wizards.com/en/rules-documents .

rules.title: Sideboard
rules.text: Extra cards that may be used to modify a deck between games of a match. See rules 100.4.

rules.title: If a player is allowed to bring a card from outside the game into a Commander game, that
rules.text:
If a player is allowed to bring a card from outside the game into a Commander game, that
player can’t bring a card into the game this way if it has the same name as a card that player had
in their starting deck, if it has the same name as a card that the player owns in the current game,
or if any color in its color identity isn’t in the color identity of the player’s commander.

rules.title: Commander Tax
rules.text:
Informal term for the additional cost to cast a commander based on the number of times a player has cast it
previously this game. See rule 903.8.

rules.title: If an effect would cause a player to take an extra turn after the current turn, but that player
rules.text:
If an effect would cause a player to take an extra turn after the current turn, but that player
wouldn’t have a turn marker at the start of that turn, that player will take the extra turn
immediately before their next turn instead.
Example:During Alex’s turn, he casts Time Walk, which causes him to take an extra
turn after this one. During the same turn, the player to Alex’s left leaves the game, which
causes the number of turn markers to be reduced. After Alex’s current turn ends, his turn
marker is removed. He won’t take the extra turn from Time Walk until just before his
normal turn the next time he receives a turn marker.

rules.title: Haste
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a creature ignore the “summoning sickness” rule. See rule 702.10, “Haste,” and
rule 302.6.

rules.title: No player receives priority during the untap step, so no spells can be cast or resolve and no
rules.text:
No player receives priority during the untap step, so no spells can be cast or resolve and no
abilities can be activated or resolve. Any ability that triggers during this step will be held until the
next time a player would receive priority, which is usually during the upkeep step. (See rule 503,
“Upkeep Step.”)

rules.title: Dies
rules.text: A creature or planeswalker “dies” if it is put into a graveyard from the battlefield. See rule 700.4.

rules.title: One card (Power Play) states that its controller is the starting player. This effect applies after
rules.text:
One card (Power Play) states that its controller is the starting player. This effect applies after
this determination has happened and supersedes these methods.

rules.title: Mill
rules.text:
To mill a number of cards, a player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard.
See rule 701.17.

rules.title: The casual variants detailed here use supplemental zones, rules, cards, and other game
rules.text:
The casual variants detailed here use supplemental zones, rules, cards, and other game
implements not used in traditionalMagicgames.

rules.title: A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t
rules.text:
A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t
be activated unless the creature has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most
recent turn began. A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control
continuously since their most recent turn began. This rule is informally called the “summoning
sickness” rule.

rules.title: Handling Illegal Actions
rules.text: Handling Illegal Actions

rules.title: First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
rules.text:
First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
dealt to a permanent is dealt to another permanent or player instead, the damage event is
modified accordingly. If the first permanent is a creature, the excess damage is the amount of
damage in excess of what would be lethal damage, taking into account damage already marked
on the creature and damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. (See rule
120.6.) Any amount of damage greater than 1 is excess damage if the source dealing that
damage to a creature has deathtouch. (See rule 702.2.) If the first permanent is a planeswalker,
the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that planeswalker’s loyalty, taking into
account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first permanent
is a battle, the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that battle’s defense, taking
into account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first
permanent has multiple card types from among the list of creature, planeswalker, and battle, the
excess damage is the greatest of the calculated amounts for each of the card types it has.

rules.title: State-Based Actions
rules.text: State-Based Actions

rules.title: Some cards refer tocommitting a crime. A player commits a crime as that player casts a spell,
rules.text:
Some cards refer tocommitting a crime. A player commits a crime as that player casts a spell,
activates an ability, or puts a triggered ability on the stack and that spell or ability targets at least
one opponent; at least one permanent, spell, or ability an opponent controls; and/or at least one card
in an opponent’s graveyard.

rules.title: To play, each player needs their own deck of traditionalMagiccards, small items to represent
rules.text:
To play, each player needs their own deck of traditionalMagiccards, small items to represent
any tokens and counters, and some way to clearly track life totals.

rules.title: Ninjutsu is an activated ability that functions only while the card with ninjutsu is in a
rules.text:
Ninjutsu is an activated ability that functions only while the card with ninjutsu is in a
player’s hand. “Ninjutsu [cost]” means “[Cost], Reveal this card from your hand, Return an
unblocked attacking creature you control to its owner’s hand: Put this card onto the battlefield
from your hand tapped and attacking.”

rules.title: Ninjutsu
rules.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature suddenly enter combat. See rule 702.49, “Ninjutsu.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: First Strike
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage before other creatures. See rule 702.7, “First
Strike.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
rules.text:

as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rule 702.4) as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that
step are those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign combat
damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike nor double
strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and blockers that
currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of combat step.

rules.title: Attacking Creature
rules.text:
A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal attack during the combat phase (once all costs to
attack, if any, have been paid), or a creature that has been put onto the battlefield attacking. It remains an
attacking creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See
rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: The card with ninjutsu remains revealed from the time the ability is announced until the
rules.text:

ability leaves the stack.

rules.title: Commander Ninjutsu
rules.text: A variant of the ninjutsu ability. See rule 702.49, “Ninjutsu.”

rules.title: Assign Combat Damage
rules.text:
To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat
Damage Step.”

rules.title: Giving double strike to a creature with first strike after it has already dealt combat damage
rules.text:
Giving double strike to a creature with first strike after it has already dealt combat damage
in the first combat damage step will allow the creature to assign combat damage in the second
combat damage step.

rules.title: Double Strike
rules.text: A keyword ability that lets a creature deal its combat damage twice. See rule 702.4, “Double Strike.”

rules.title: Giving first strike to a creature without it after combat damage has already been dealt in the
rules.text:
Giving first strike to a creature without it after combat damage has already been dealt in the
first combat damage step won’t preclude that creature from assigning combat damage in the
second combat damage step. Removing first strike from a creature after it has already dealt
combat damage in the first combat damage step won’t allow it to also assign combat damage in
the second combat damage step (unless the creature has double strike).

rules.title: Declare Attackers
rules.text:
To choose a set of creatures that will attack, declare whether each creature is attacking the defending player
or a planeswalker that player controls, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to attack. See
rule 508.1.

rules.title: First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
rules.text:
First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step. (See rule
510, “Combat Damage Step.”)

rules.title: Combat Damage Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the fourth step of the combat phase. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: Removing double strike from a creature during the first combat damage step will stop it
rules.text:
Removing double strike from a creature during the first combat damage step will stop it
from assigning combat damage in the second combat damage step.

rules.title: Declare Attackers Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the second step of the combat phase. See rule 508, “Declare Attackers Step.”

rules.title: Combat Damage
rules.text:
Damage dealt during the combat damage step by attacking creatures and blocking creatures as a
consequence of combat. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: Commander ninjutsu is a variant of the ninjutsu ability that also functions while the card
rules.text:

with commander ninjutsu is in the command zone. “Commander ninjutsu [cost]” means “[Cost],
Reveal this card from your hand or from the command zone, Return an unblocked attacking
creature you control to its owner’s hand: Put this card onto the battlefield tapped and attacking.”

rules.title: Delayed Triggered Ability
rules.text:
An ability created by effects generated when some spells or abilities resolve, or when some replacement
effects are applied, that does something later on rather than at that time. See rule 603.7.

rules.title: First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then
rules.text:

the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-
based action doesn’t use the stack. A player assigns a creature’s combat damage according to the
following rules:

rules.text:

117.7.

rules.text:

will assign its combat damage. Then the defending team announces how each blocking creature
will assign its combat damage. See rule 510.1.

rules.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would
be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

rules.title: Indestructible
rules.text: A keyword ability that precludes a permanent from being destroyed. See rule 702.12.

rules.title: A permanent with indestructible can’t be destroyed. Such permanents aren’t destroyed by
rules.text:
A permanent with indestructible can’t be destroyed. Such permanents aren’t destroyed by
lethal damage, and they ignore the state-based action that checks for lethal damage (see rule
704.5g).

rules.title: Toughness
rules.text:
1. Part of a card that only creature cards have. A creature card’s toughness is printed after the slash in its
lower right corner. See rule 208, “Power/Toughness.”
2. A characteristic that only creatures have. See rule 302.4.

rules.title: If a creature has toughness greater than 0, and it’s been dealt damage by a source with
rules.text:
If a creature has toughness greater than 0, and it’s been dealt damage by a source with
deathtouch since the last time state-based actions were checked, that creature is destroyed.
Regeneration can replace this event.

rules.title: Base Power, Base Toughness
rules.text:
Effects that change the base power and/or base toughness of a creature set one or both of those values to a
specific number. See rule 613, “Interaction of Continuous Effects.”

rules.title: Unlike triggered abilities, state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the
rules.text:
Unlike triggered abilities, state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the
resolution of a spell or ability.
Example:A player controls Maro, a creature with the ability “Maro’s power and toughness
are each equal to the number of cards in your hand” and casts a spell whose effect is
“Discard your hand, then draw seven cards.” Maro will temporarily have toughness 0 in the
middle of the spell’s resolution but will be back up to toughness 7 when the spell finishes
resolving. Thus Maro will survive when state-based actions are checked. In contrast, an
ability that triggers when the player has no cards in hand goes on the stack after the spell
resolves, because its trigger event happened during resolution.

rules.title: Damage
rules.text:
Objects can deal “damage” to creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the
object or player that receives that damage. See rule 120, “Damage.”

rules.title: If a state-based action results in a permanent leaving the battlefield at the same time other state-
rules.text:
If a state-based action results in a permanent leaving the battlefield at the same time other state-
based actions were performed, that permanent’s last known information is derived from the game
state before any of those state-based actions were performed.
Example:You control Young Wolf, a 1/1 creature with undying, and it has a +1/+1 counter
on it. A spell puts three -1/-1 counters on Young Wolf. Before state-based actions are
performed, Young Wolf has one +1/+1 counter and three -1/-1 counters on it. After state-
based actions are performed, Young Wolf is in the graveyard. When it was last on the
battlefield, it had a +1/+1 counter on it, so undying will not trigger.

rules.title: Remove from Combat
rules.text:
Certain events can cause an attacking or blocking creature, or a planeswalker that’s being attacked, to be
“removed from combat.” A permanent that’s removed from combat has no further involvement in that
combat phase. See rule 506.4.

rules.text:

(see rule 120.3). If the total damage marked on that creature is greater than or equal to its toughness,
that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed as a state-based action (see rule 704). All
damage marked on a creature is removed when it regenerates (see rule 701.19, “Regenerate”) and
during the cleanup step (see rule 514.2).

rules.title: Dethrone
rules.text:

rules.title: Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
that damage doesn’t destroy it. Rather, state-based actions may destroy a creature or otherwise put a
permanent into its owner’s graveyard, due to the results of the damage dealt to that permanent. See

Example:A player casts Lightning Bolt, an instant that says “Lightning Bolt deals 3
damage to any target,” targeting a 2/2 creature. After Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to that
creature, the creature is destroyed as a state-based action. Neither Lightning Bolt nor the
damage dealt by Lightning Bolt destroyed that creature.

rules.title: Decayed
rules.text:

during the cleanup step (see rule 514.2).
