rules.title: If an attacking creature with trample or trample over planeswalkers is blocked, but there
rules.text:
If an attacking creature with trample or trample over planeswalkers is blocked, but there
are no creatures blocking it when damage is assigned, its damage is assigned to the defending
player and/or planeswalker as though all blocking creatures have been assigned lethal damage.

rules.title: Blocked Creature
rules.text:
An attacking creature that another creature blocks or that an effect causes to become blocked. It remains a
blocked creature until it’s removed from combat, an effect says that it becomes unblocked, or the combat
phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

rules.title: If a creature with trample over planeswalkers is attacking a planeswalker and that
rules.text:
If a creature with trample over planeswalkers is attacking a planeswalker and that
planeswalker is removed from combat, the creature’s damage may be assigned to the defending
player once all blocking creatures have been dealt lethal damage or, if there are no blocking
creatures when damage is assigned, all its damage is assigned to the defending player. This is an
exception to rule 506.4c, and it does not cause the creature to be attacking that player.

rules.title: Unblocked Creature
rules.text:
An attacking creature once no creature has been declared as a blocker for it, unless an effect has caused it to
become blocked. It remains an unblocked creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase
ends, whichever comes first. See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

rules.title: An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s
rules.text:
An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s
attacking. If it isn’t currently attacking anything (if, for example, it was attacking a
planeswalker that has left the battlefield), it assigns no combat damage.

rules.title: Block
rules.text:
To send a creature into combat defensively. A creature can block an attacking creature. See rule 509,
“Declare Blockers Step.”

rules.title: The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
rules.text:
The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
blocking it. Once all those blocking creatures are assigned lethal damage, any excess damage is
assigned as its controller chooses among those blocking creatures and the player, planeswalker,
or battle the creature is attacking. When checking for assigned lethal damage, take into account
damage already marked on the creature and damage from other creatures that’s being assigned
during the same combat damage step, but not any abilities or effects that might change the
amount of damage that’s actually dealt. The attacking creature’s controller need not assign
lethal damage to all those blocking creatures but in that case can’t assign any damage to the
player or planeswalker it’s attacking.
Example:A 2/2 creature that can block an additional creature blocks two attackers: a
1/1 with no abilities and a 3/3 with trample. The active player could assign 1 damage
from the first attacker and 1 damage from the second to the blocking creature, and 2
damage to the defending player from the creature with trample.
Example:A 6/6 green creature with trample is blocked by a 2/2 creature with protection
from green. The attacking creature’s controller must assign at least 2 damage to the
blocker, even though that damage will be prevented by the blocker’s protection ability.
The attacking creature’s controller can divide the rest of the damage as they choose
between the blocking creature and the defending player.

rules.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would
be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

rules.title: If a creature is attacking a planeswalker or battle, removing that planeswalker or battle from
rules.text:
If a creature is attacking a planeswalker or battle, removing that planeswalker or battle from
combat doesn’t remove that creature from combat. It continues to be an attacking creature,
although it is not attacking any player, planeswalker, or battle. It may be blocked. If it is
unblocked, it will deal no combat damage.

rules.title: Assign Combat Damage
rules.text:
To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat
Damage Step.”

rules.title: A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
rules.text:
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
currently blocking it (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it assigns
no combat damage. If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that
creature. If two or more creatures are blocking it, it assigns its combat damage to those creatures
divided as its controller chooses among them.
Example:An attacking Elvish Regrower (a 4/3 creature) is blocked by Vampire Spawn
(a 2/3 creature) and Helpful Hunter (a 1/1 creature). Elvish Regrower’s controller can
assign all 4 damage to the Hunter, 1 damage to the Spawn and 3 damage to the Hunter,
2 damage to each creature, 3 damage to the Spawn and 1 damage to the Hunter, or all 4
damage to the Spawn.

rules.title: Remove from Combat
rules.text:
Certain events can cause an attacking or blocking creature, or a planeswalker that’s being attacked, to be
“removed from combat.” A permanent that’s removed from combat has no further involvement in that
combat phase. See rule 506.4.

rules.title: A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
rules.text:
A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
blocking any creatures (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it
assigns no combat damage. If it’s blocking exactly one creature, it assigns all its combat damage
to that creature. If it’s blocking two or more creatures, it assigns its combat damage divided as
its controller chooses among them.

rules.title: Blocking Creature
rules.text:
A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal block during the combat phase (once all costs to
block, if any, have been paid), or a creature that has been put onto the battlefield blocking. It remains a
blocking creature until it’s removed from combat or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. See rule
509, “Declare Blockers Step.”

rules.title: If a creature without trample over planeswalkers is attacking a planeswalker, none of its
rules.text:
If a creature without trample over planeswalkers is attacking a planeswalker, none of its
combat damage can be assigned to the defending player, even if that planeswalker has been
removed from combat or the damage the attacking creature could assign is greater than the
planeswalker’s loyalty.

rules.title: Combat Damage
rules.text:
Damage dealt during the combat damage step by attacking creatures and blocking creatures as a
consequence of combat. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: Trample Over Planeswalkers
rules.text:
A variant of trample that modifies how a creature assigns combat damage if it’s attacking a planeswalker.
See rule 702.19, “Trample”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rule 702.4) as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that
step are those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign combat
damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike nor double
strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and blockers that
currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of combat step.

rules.title: Attacks and Isn’t Blocked
rules.text:
An ability that triggers when a creature “attacks and isn’t blocked” triggers when the creature becomes an
unblocked attacking creature. See rule 509.1h.

rules.title: An attacking creature with one or more creatures declared as blockers for it becomes a
rules.text:
An attacking creature with one or more creatures declared as blockers for it becomes a
blocked creature; one with no creatures declared as blockers for it becomes an unblocked
creature. This remains unchanged until the creature is removed from combat, an effect says that
it becomes blocked or unblocked, or the combat phase ends, whichever comes first. A creature
remains blocked even if all the creatures blocking it are removed from combat.

rules.title: Block Alone
rules.text:
A creature “blocks alone” if it’s the only creature declared as a blocker during the declare blockers step. A
creature “is blocking alone” if it’s blocking but no other creatures are. See rule 506.5.

rules.title: Block
rules.text:
To send a creature into combat defensively. A creature can block an attacking creature. See rule 509,
“Declare Blockers Step.”

rules.title: Damage dealt to a creature by a source with neither wither nor infect is marked on that creature
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature by a source with neither wither nor infect is marked on that creature
(see rule 120.3). If the total damage marked on that creature is greater than or equal to its toughness,
that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed as a state-based action (see rule 704). All
damage marked on a creature is removed when it regenerates (see rule 701.19, “Regenerate”) and
during the cleanup step (see rule 514.2).

rules.title: Dethrone
rules.text:

rule 702.105, “Dethrone.”

rules.title: A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
rules.text:
A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
blocking any creatures (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it
assigns no combat damage. If it’s blocking exactly one creature, it assigns all its combat damage
to that creature. If it’s blocking two or more creatures, it assigns its combat damage divided as
its controller chooses among them.

rules.title: Declare Blockers
rules.text:
To choose a set of creatures that will block, declare which attacking creature each creature is blocking, and
pay any costs required to allow those creatures to block. See rule 509.1.

rules.title: First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
rules.text:
First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
dealt to a permanent is dealt to another permanent or player instead, the damage event is
modified accordingly. If the first permanent is a creature, the excess damage is the amount of
damage in excess of what would be lethal damage, taking into account damage already marked
on the creature and damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. (See rule
120.6.) Any amount of damage greater than 1 is excess damage if the source dealing that
damage to a creature has deathtouch. (See rule 702.2.) If the first permanent is a planeswalker,
the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that planeswalker’s loyalty, taking into
account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first permanent
is a battle, the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that battle’s defense, taking
into account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first
permanent has multiple card types from among the list of creature, planeswalker, and battle, the
excess damage is the greatest of the calculated amounts for each of the card types it has.

rules.text:

citations.title: The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
citations.excerpt:
The controller of an attacking creature with trample first assigns damage to the creature(s)
blocking it. Once all those blocking creatures are assigned lethal damage, any excess damage is
assigned as its controller chooses among those blocking creatures and the player, planeswalker,
or battle the creature is attacking. When checking for assigned lethal damage, take into account
damage already marked on the creature and damage from other creatures that’s being assigned
during the same combat damage step, but not any abilities or effects that might change the
amount of damage that’s actually dealt. The attacking creature’s controller need not assign
lethal damage to all those blocking creatures but in that case can’t assign any damage to the
player or planeswalker it’s attacking.
Example:A 2/2 creature that can block an additional creature blocks two attackers: a
1/1 with no abilities and a 3/3 with trample. The active player could assign 1 damage
from the first attacker and 1 damage from the second to the blocking creature, and 2
damage to the defending player from the creature with trample.
Example:A 6/6 green creature with trample is blocked by a 2/2 creature with protection
from green. The attacking creature’s controller must assign at least 2 damage to the
blocker, even though that damage will be prevented by the blocker’s protection ability.
The attacking creature’s controller can divide the rest of the damage as they choose
between the blocking creature and the defending player.

rules.title: Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
that damage doesn’t destroy it. Rather, state-based actions may destroy a creature or otherwise put a
permanent into its owner’s graveyard, due to the results of the damage dealt to that permanent. See
rule 704.
Example:A player casts Lightning Bolt, an instant that says “Lightning Bolt deals 3
damage to any target,” targeting a 2/2 creature. After Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to that
creature, the creature is destroyed as a state-based action. Neither Lightning Bolt nor the
damage dealt by Lightning Bolt destroyed that creature.

rules.text:

rules.text:

be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

foreignNames.name: Fulmine
foreignNames.text: Il Fulmine infligge 3 danni a un qualsiasi bersaglio.
foreignNames.flavor: Il magoscintilla urlò, facendo appello all'ira delle tempeste della sua giovinezza. Con sua gran sorpresa, il cielo rispose con un'intensa energia che non pensava di rivedere mai più.

rules.title: Immediately after combat damage has been assigned during the combat damage step, all
rules.text:
Immediately after combat damage has been assigned during the combat damage step, all
combat damage is dealt simultaneously. See rule 510.2.

rules.title: Assign Combat Damage
rules.text:
To determine how an attacking or blocking creature will deal its combat damage. See rule 510, “Combat
Damage Step.”

rules.title: Any object can deal damage.
rules.text: Any object can deal damage.

rules.title: Damage
rules.text:
Objects can deal “damage” to creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the
object or player that receives that damage. See rule 120, “Damage.”

rules.title: Second, damage is dealt, as modified by replacement and prevention effects that interact
rules.text:
Second, damage is dealt, as modified by replacement and prevention effects that interact
with damage. (See rule 614, “Replacement Effects,” and rule 615, “Prevention Effects.”)
Abilities that trigger when damage is dealt trigger now and wait to be put on the stack.

rules.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would
be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

rules.title: Objects can dealdamageto battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally
rules.text:
Objects can dealdamageto battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally
detrimental to the object or player that receives that damage. An object that deals damage is the
sourceof that damage.

rules.title: First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then
rules.text:
First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then
the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-
based action doesn’t use the stack. A player assigns a creature’s combat damage according to the
following rules:

rules.title: Combat Damage
rules.text:
Damage dealt during the combat damage step by attacking creatures and blocking creatures as a
consequence of combat. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike or double strike (see rule 702.4)
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action
rules.text:
Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action
doesn’t use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time
combat damage is assigned and the time it’s dealt.

rules.title: Combat Damage Step
rules.text: Part of the turn. This step is the fourth step of the combat phase. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike (see
rule 702.4) as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that
step are those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign combat
damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike nor double
strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and blockers that
currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of combat step.

rules.title: Source of Damage
rules.text: The object that dealt that damage. See rule 609.7.

rules.title: Combat damage is assigned in APNAP order. Other than that, the combat damage step proceeds
rules.text:
Combat damage is assigned in APNAP order. Other than that, the combat damage step proceeds
just as in a two-player game. See rule 510, “Combat Damage Step.”

rules.title: In Response To
rules.text:
An instant spell that’s been cast, or an activated ability that’s been activated, while another spell or ability
is on the stack has been cast or activated “in response to” the earlier spell or ability. See rule 117.7.

rules.title: If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
rules.text:
If at least one attacking or blocking creature has first strike (see rule 702.7) or double strike
as the combat damage step begins, the only creatures that assign combat damage in that step are
those with first strike or double strike. After that step, instead of proceeding to the end of
combat step, the phase gets a second combat damage step. The only creatures that assign
combat damage in that step are the remaining attackers and blockers that had neither first strike
nor double strike as the first combat damage step began, as well as the remaining attackers and
blockers that currently have double strike. After that step, the phase proceeds to the end of
combat step.

rules.title: Declare Attackers

To choose a set of creatures that will attack, declare whether each creature is attacking the defending player
or a planeswalker that player controls, and pay any costs required to allow those creatures to attack. See
rule 508.1.

rules.text:

effects are applied, that does something later on rather than at that time. See rule 603.7.

rules.title: A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
rules.text:
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it. If no creatures are
currently blocking it (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it assigns
no combat damage. If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that
creature. If two or more creatures are blocking it, it assigns its combat damage to those creatures
divided as its controller chooses among them.
Example:An attacking Elvish Regrower (a 4/3 creature) is blocked by Vampire Spawn
(a 2/3 creature) and Helpful Hunter (a 1/1 creature). Elvish Regrower’s controller can
assign all 4 damage to the Hunter, 1 damage to the Spawn and 3 damage to the Hunter,
2 damage to each creature, 3 damage to the Spawn and 1 damage to the Hunter, or all 4
damage to the Spawn.

rules.title: A blocking creature assigns combat damage to the creatures it’s blocking. If it isn’t currently
rules.text:

blocking any creatures (if, for example, they were destroyed or removed from combat), it
assigns no combat damage. If it’s blocking exactly one creature, it assigns all its combat damage
to that creature. If it’s blocking two or more creatures, it assigns its combat damage divided as

turns.question: If a creature activates an ordinary non-mana ability and is destroyed in response, does that alone remove its ability from the stack?

result.answer: No. Once the non-mana ability is activated, it exists on the stack independently of its creature source, and destroying the creature afterward does not affect the ability. [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:113.7a] [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:605.3b]

claims.text: No. Once the non-mana ability is activated, it exists on the stack independently of its creature source, and destroying the creature afterward does not affect the ability.
No. Once the non-mana ability is activated, it exists on the stack independently of its creature source, and destroying the creature afterward does not affect the ability.

rules.title: Once activated or triggered, an ability exists on the stack independently of its source.
rules.text:
Once activated or triggered, an ability exists on the stack independently of its source.
Destruction or removal of the source after that time won’t affect the ability. Note that some
abilities cause a source to do something (for example, “This creature deals 1 damage to any
target”) rather than the ability doing anything directly. In these cases, any activated or triggered
ability that references information about the source for use while announcing an activated
ability or putting a triggered ability on the stack checks that information when the ability is put
onto the stack. Otherwise, it will check that information when it resolves. In both instances, if
the source is no longer in the zone it’s expected to be in at that time, its last known information
is used. The source can still perform the action even though it no longer exists.

rules.title: Activate
rules.text:
To put an activated ability onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve and have its
effect. See rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: An activated mana ability doesn’t go on the stack, so it can’t be targeted, countered, or
rules.text:
An activated mana ability doesn’t go on the stack, so it can’t be targeted, countered, or
otherwise responded to. Rather, it resolves immediately after it is activated. (See rule 405.6c.)

rules.title: Mana Ability
rules.text:
An activated or triggered ability that could create mana and doesn’t use the stack. See rule 605, “Mana
Abilities.”

rules.title: To activate an ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve
rules.text:
To activate an ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will eventually resolve
and have its effect. Only an object’s controller (or its owner, if it doesn’t have a controller) can
activate its activated ability unless the object specifically says otherwise. Activating an ability
follows the steps listed below, in order. If, at any point during the activation of an ability, a player is
unable to comply with any of those steps, the activation is illegal; the game returns to the moment
before that ability started to be activated (see rule 733, “Handling Illegal Actions”). Announcements
and payments can’t be altered after they’ve been made.

rules.title: Activated Ability
rules.text:
A kind of ability. Activated abilities are written as “[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]” See
rule 113, “Abilities,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: Some activated abilities and some triggered abilities aremana abilities. Mana abilities follow
rules.text:
Some activated abilities and some triggered abilities aremana abilities. Mana abilities follow
special rules: They don’t use the stack, and, under certain circumstances, a player can activate mana
abilities even if they don’t have priority. See rule 605, “Mana Abilities.”

rules.title: Mana Source (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete card type. All cards printed with this card type are now instants. All abilities that, as printed,
said a player could “play as a mana source” are now mana abilities. All relevant cards have been given
errata in the Oracle card reference.

rules.title: To activate an activated ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will
rules.text:
To activate an activated ability is to put it onto the stack and pay its costs, so that it will
eventually resolve and have its effect. Only an object’s controller (or its owner, if it doesn’t
have a controller) can activate its activated ability unless the object specifically says otherwise.
A player may activate an ability if they have priority. See rule 602, “Activating Activated
Abilities.”

rules.title: Trigger
rules.text:
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically
“triggers.” That means its controller puts it on the stack the next time a player would receive priority. See
rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities.”

rules.title: Thesourceof an ability is the object that generated it. The source of an activated ability on the
rules.text:
Thesourceof an ability is the object that generated it. The source of an activated ability on the
stack is the object whose ability was activated. The source of a triggered ability (other than a
delayed triggered ability) on the stack, or one that has triggered and is waiting to be put on the
stack, is the object whose ability triggered. To determine the source of a delayed triggered ability,
see rules 603.7d–f.

rules.title: Ability
rules.text:
1. Text on an object that explains what that object does or can do.
2. An activated or triggered ability on the stack. This kind of ability is an object.
See rule 113, “Abilities,” and section 6, “Spells, Abilities, and Effects.”

rules.title: Activating an activated mana ability follows the rules for activating any other activated ability
rules.text:
Activating an activated mana ability follows the rules for activating any other activated ability
(see rule 602.2), with the following exceptions:

rules.title: Respond
rules.text:
To cast an instant spell or activate an ability while another spell or ability is already on the stack. See rule
117.7.

rules.title: The player announces that they are activating the ability. If an activated ability is being
rules.text:
The player announces that they are activating the ability. If an activated ability is being
activated from a hidden zone, the card that has that ability is revealed (see rule 701.20a). That
ability is created on the stack as an object that’s not a card. It becomes the topmost object on the
stack. It has the text of the ability that created it, and no other characteristics. Its controller is the
player who activated the ability. The ability remains on the stack until it’s countered, it resolves,
or an effect moves it elsewhere.

rules.title: Resolve
rules.text:
When the spell or ability on top of the stack “resolves,” its instructions are followed and it has its effect.
See rule 608, “Resolving Spells and Abilities.”

rules.title: Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the
rules.text:
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the
next time a player would receive priority. See rule 117, “Timing and Priority.” The ability becomes
the topmost object on the stack. It has the text of the ability that created it, and no other
characteristics. It remains on the stack until it’s countered, it resolves, a rule causes it to be removed
from the stack, or an effect moves it elsewhere.

rules.title: Destroy
rules.text: To move a permanent from the battlefield to its owner’s graveyard. See rule 701.8, “Destroy.”

rules.title: An ability can be an activated or triggered ability on the stack. This kind of ability is an
rules.text:
An ability can be an activated or triggered ability on the stack. This kind of ability is an
object. (See section 6, “Spells, Abilities, and Effects.”)

rules.title: Activation Cost
rules.text:
Everything that appears before the colon in an activated ability’s text. It must be paid to activate the ability.
See rule 118, “Costs,” and rule 602, “Activating Activated Abilities.”

rules.title: The controller of an activated ability on the stack is the player who activated it. The controller of
rules.text:
The controller of an activated ability on the stack is the player who activated it. The controller of
a triggered ability on the stack (other than a delayed triggered ability) is the player who controlled
the ability’s source when it triggered, or, if it had no controller, the player who owned the ability’s
source when it triggered. To determine the controller of a delayed triggered ability, see rules
603.7d–f.

rules.title: Source of Mana
rules.text: The spell that produced mana or the source of the ability that produced mana. See rule 106.3.

rules.title: Activating an ability that alters costs won’t affect spells and abilities that are already on the
rules.text:
Activating an ability that alters costs won’t affect spells and abilities that are already on the
stack.

rules.title: Delayed Triggered Ability
rules.text:
An ability created by effects generated when some spells or abilities resolve, or when some replacement
effects are applied, that does something later on rather than at that time. See rule 603.7.

Mana abilities resolve immediately. If a mana ability both produces mana and has another
effect, the mana is produced and the other effect happens immediately. If a player had priority
before a mana ability was activated, that player gets priority after it resolves. (See rule 605,
“Mana Abilities.”)

result.answer: A permanent is a card or token on the battlefield. It remains there indefinitely unless an effect or rule moves it to another zone. [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:glossary:Permanent] [mtg:April%2017%2C%202026:rule:110.1]

claims.text: A permanent is a card or token on the battlefield. It remains there indefinitely unless an effect or rule moves it to another zone.

rules.title: The term “permanent spell” is used to refer to a spell that will enter the battlefield as a
rules.text:
The term “permanent spell” is used to refer to a spell that will enter the battlefield as a
permanent as part of its resolution. Specifically, it means an artifact, battle, creature,
enchantment, or planeswalker spell.

rules.title: Permanent Spell
rules.text: A spell that will enter the battlefield as a permanent as part of its resolution. See rule 110.4b.

rules.title: Permanents
rules.text: Permanents

rules.title: Permanent
rules.text: A card or token on the battlefield. See rule 110, “Permanents.”

rules.title: The term “permanent card” is used to refer to a card that could be put onto the battlefield.
rules.text:
The term “permanent card” is used to refer to a card that could be put onto the battlefield.
Specifically, it means an artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land, or planeswalker card.

rules.title: Permanently (Obsolete)
rules.text:
An obsolete term used to indicate that a continuous effect has no duration and thus lasts until the end of the
game. Cards printed with this term have received errata in the Oracle card reference to delete it.

rules.title: Apermanentis a card or token on the battlefield. A permanent remains on the battlefield
rules.text:
Apermanentis a card or token on the battlefield. A permanent remains on the battlefield
indefinitely. A card or token becomes a permanent as it enters the battlefield and it stops being a
permanent as it’s moved to another zone by an effect or rule.

rules.title: Merged Permanent
rules.text:
A card or token may merge with a permanent to form a merged permanent. This merged permanent is
represented by more than one card and/or token. See rule 730, “Merging with Permanents.”

rules.title: If a permanent somehow loses all its permanent types, it remains on the battlefield. It’s still a
rules.text:
If a permanent somehow loses all its permanent types, it remains on the battlefield. It’s still a
permanent.

rules.title: Indestructible
rules.text: A keyword ability that precludes a permanent from being destroyed. See rule 702.12.

rules.title: A permanent retains its status until a spell, ability, or turn-based action changes it, even if
rules.text:
A permanent retains its status until a spell, ability, or turn-based action changes it, even if
that status is not relevant to it.
Example:Dimir Doppelganger says “{1}{U}{B}: Exile target creature card from a
graveyard. This creature becomes a copy of that card, except it has this ability.” It
becomes a copy of Jushi Apprentice, a flip card. Through use of Jushi Apprentice’s
ability, this creature flips, making it a copy of Tomoya the Revealer with the Dimir
Doppelganger ability. If this permanent then becomes a copy of Runeclaw Bear, it will
retain its flipped status even though that has no relevance to Runeclaw Bear. If its copy
ability is activated again, this time targeting a Nezumi Shortfang card (another flip
card), this permanent’s flipped status means it will have the characteristics of
Stabwhisker the Odious (the flipped version of Nezumi Shortfang) with the Dimir
Doppelganger ability.

rules.title: Sorcery
rules.text: A card type. A sorcery is not a permanent. See rule 307, “Sorceries.”

rules.title: Permanents exist only on the battlefield. Every object on the battlefield is a permanent. See rule
rules.text:
Permanents exist only on the battlefield. Every object on the battlefield is a permanent. See rule
110, “Permanents.”

rules.title: Finality Counter
rules.text:
A counter that exiles the permanent it is on if that permanent would go to the graveyard from the
battlefield. See rule 122.1h.

rules.title: Some spells and abilities refer to a “transformed permanent.” This phrase refers to a
rules.text:
Some spells and abilities refer to a “transformed permanent.” This phrase refers to a
double-faced permanent on the battlefield with its back face up. A permanent with its front face
up is never considered a transformed permanent, even if it had its back face up previously.
Similarly, an object represented by more than one card, such as a melded or merged permanent,
is never considered a transformed permanent, even if it has components that are back face up.
See rules 701.42, “Meld,” and 730, “Merging with Permanents.”

rules.title: Vanishing
rules.text:
A keyword ability that limits how long a permanent remains on the battlefield. See rule 702.63,
“Vanishing.”

rules.title: A spell or permanent “escaped” if that spell or the spell that became that permanent as it
rules.text:
A spell or permanent “escaped” if that spell or the spell that became that permanent as it
resolved was cast from a graveyard with an escape ability.

rules.title: Eternalize
rules.text:
A keyword ability that lets a player exile a creature card from their graveyard to create an eternalized token
version of that card. See rule 702.129, “Eternalize.”

rules.title: Permanents enter the battlefield untapped, unflipped, face up, and phased in unless a spell or
rules.text:
Permanents enter the battlefield untapped, unflipped, face up, and phased in unless a spell or
ability says otherwise.

rules.title: Enchantment
rules.text: A card type. An enchantment is a permanent. See rule 303, “Enchantments.” See also Aura.

rules.title: Some cards refer tomodifiedpermanents. A permanent is modified if it has one or more counters
rules.text:
Some cards refer tomodifiedpermanents. A permanent is modified if it has one or more counters
on it (see rule 122), if it is equipped (see rule 301.5), or if it is enchanted by an Aura that is
controlled by that permanent’s controller (see rule 303.4).

rules.title: Warp
rules.text:
A keyword ability found on permanent cards that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule
702.185, “Warp.”

rules.title: Flipping a permanent is a one-way process. Once a permanent is flipped, it’s impossible for it to
rules.text:
Flipping a permanent is a one-way process. Once a permanent is flipped, it’s impossible for it to
become unflipped. However, if a flipped permanent leaves the battlefield, it retains no memory of
its status. See rule 110.5.

rules.title: Persist
rules.text:
A keyword ability that can return a creature from the graveyard to the battlefield. See rule 702.79,
“Persist.”

rules.title: There are six permanent types: artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land, and planeswalker.
rules.text:
There are six permanent types: artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land, and planeswalker.
Instant and sorcery cards can’t enter the battlefield and thus can’t be permanents. Some kindred
cards can enter the battlefield and some can’t, depending on their other card types. See section 3,
“Card Types.”

rules.title: Planeswalker
rules.text: A card type. A planeswalker is a permanent. See rule 306, “Planeswalkers.”

rules.title: Face-Down Spells and Permanents
rules.text: Face-Down Spells and Permanents

rules.title: Creature
rules.text: A card type. A creature is a permanent. See rule 302, “Creatures.”

rules.title: An ability of a permanent may refer to the exiled cards used to craft it. This refers to cards
rules.text:
An ability of a permanent may refer to the exiled cards used to craft it. This refers to cards
in exile that were exiled to pay the activation cost of the craft ability that put this permanent
onto the battlefield.

rules.title: Prepared
rules.text:
A designation a permanent may have that allows you to cast a copy of that card with its alternative
characteristics. See rule 722, “Preparation Cards.”

rules.title: The only ways a permanent can be destroyed are as a result of an effect that uses the word
rules.text:
The only ways a permanent can be destroyed are as a result of an effect that uses the word
“destroy” or as a result of the state-based actions that check for lethal damage (see rule 704.5g)
or damage from a source with deathtouch (see rule 704.5h). If a permanent is put into its
owner’s graveyard for any other reason, it hasn’t been “destroyed.”

rules.title: Damage dealt to a creature by a source with neither wither nor infect is marked on that creature
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature by a source with neither wither nor infect is marked on that creature
(see rule 120.3). If the total damage marked on that creature is greater than or equal to its toughness,
that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed as a state-based action (see rule 704). All
damage marked on a creature is removed when it regenerates (see rule 701.19, “Regenerate”) and
during the cleanup step (see rule 514.2).

rules.title: Annihilator

rules.title: Damage
rules.text:
Objects can deal “damage” to creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the
object or player that receives that damage. See rule 120, “Damage.”

rules.text:
If a creature has toughness greater than 0, it has damage marked on it, and the total damage
marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage
and is destroyed. Regeneration can replace this event.

rules.title: Destroy
rules.text: To move a permanent from the battlefield to its owner’s graveyard. See rule 701.8, “Destroy.”

rules.title: Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
rules.text:
Damage dealt to a creature, planeswalker, or battle doesn’t destroy it. Likewise, the source of
that damage doesn’t destroy it. Rather, state-based actions may destroy a creature or otherwise put a
permanent into its owner’s graveyard, due to the results of the damage dealt to that permanent. See
rule 704.
Example:A player casts Lightning Bolt, an instant that says “Lightning Bolt deals 3
damage to any target,” targeting a 2/2 creature. After Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to that
creature, the creature is destroyed as a state-based action. Neither Lightning Bolt nor the
damage dealt by Lightning Bolt destroyed that creature.

rules.title: Dethrone

rule 702.105, “Dethrone.”

rules.title: Damage marked on a creature remains until the cleanup step, even if that permanent stops being
rules.text:
Damage marked on a creature remains until the cleanup step, even if that permanent stops being
a creature. If the total damage marked on a creature is greater than or equal to its toughness, that
creature has been dealtlethal damageand is destroyed as a state-based action (see rule 704). All
damage marked on a permanent is removed when it regenerates (see rule 701.19, “Regenerate”) and
during the cleanup step (see rule 514.2).

rules.title: Any nonzero amount of combat damage assigned to a creature by a source with deathtouch
rules.text:
Any nonzero amount of combat damage assigned to a creature by a source with deathtouch
is considered to be lethal damage for the purposes of determining if excess damage is being
dealt.

rules.title: Damage Assignment Order (Obsolete)
rules.text:
Previously, if a creature blocks or becomes blocked by multiple creatures, the creature’s controller would
be required to choose an order in which it would assign combat damage to the creatures blocking or
blocked by it. Now, its controller no longer needs to assign an order, and simply divides its combat damage
as they choose among all creatures it’s blocking or blocked by. See rules 510.1c-d.

rules.title: First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
rules.text:
First, if an effect that’s causing damage to be dealt states thatexcess damagethat would be
dealt to a permanent is dealt to another permanent or player instead, the damage event is
modified accordingly. If the first permanent is a creature, the excess damage is the amount of
damage in excess of what would be lethal damage, taking into account damage already marked
on the creature and damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. (See rule
120.6.) Any amount of damage greater than 1 is excess damage if the source dealing that
damage to a creature has deathtouch. (See rule 702.2.) If the first permanent is a planeswalker,
the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that planeswalker’s loyalty, taking into
account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first permanent
is a battle, the excess damage is the amount of damage in excess of that battle’s defense, taking
into account damage from other sources that would be dealt at the same time. If the first
permanent has multiple card types from among the list of creature, planeswalker, and battle, the
excess damage is the greatest of the calculated amounts for each of the card types it has.

rules.title: Unlike triggered abilities, state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the
rules.text:
Unlike triggered abilities, state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the
resolution of a spell or ability.
Example:A player controls Maro, a creature with the ability “Maro’s power and toughness
are each equal to the number of cards in your hand” and casts a spell whose effect is
“Discard your hand, then draw seven cards.” Maro will temporarily have toughness 0 in the
middle of the spell’s resolution but will be back up to toughness 7 when the spell finishes
resolving. Thus Maro will survive when state-based actions are checked. In contrast, an
ability that triggers when the player has no cards in hand goes on the stack after the spell
resolves, because its trigger event happened during resolution.

foreignNames.name: Wolkenwaldläufer
foreignNames.text: {T}: Du kannst eine Länderkarte aus deiner Hand ins Spiel bringen. Spiele diese Fähigkeit nur zu einem Zeitpunkt, zu dem du auch eine Hexerei spielen könntest.
foreignNames.flavor: Noch nicht einmal die Elfen kennen den Wolkenwald genau. Ihre Waldläufer sind lediglich am besten dafür gerüstet, mit seinen vielen Geheimnissen umzugehen.

foreignNames.name: Explorador de Veloceleste
foreignNames.text: {T}: Puedes poner en juego una carta de tierra de tu mano. Juega esta habilidad sólo cuando puedas jugar un conjuro.
foreignNames.flavor: Ni siquiera los elfos conocen verdaderamente el bosque de Veloceleste. Los exploradores son simplemente los mejor equipados para manejar sus incertidumbres.

foreignNames.name: Ranger de Linciel
foreignNames.text: {T} : Vous pouvez mettre en jeu une carte de terrain de votre main. Ne jouez cette capacité que lorsque vous pourriez jouer un rituel.
foreignNames.flavor: Même les elfes ne connaissent pas vraiment la forêt de Linciel. Les rangers sont simplement les mieux équipés pour affronter ses mystères.

foreignNames.name: Ranger di Cielsudario
foreignNames.text: {T}: Puoi mettere in gioco una carta terra dalla tua mano. Gioca questa abilità solo quando potresti giocare una stregoneria.
foreignNames.flavor: Neppure gli elfi conoscono realmente la Foresta di Cielsudario. I ranger sono sì e no i meglio equipaggiati per affrontare la sua incertezza.

foreignNames.name: スカイシュラウドのレインジャー
foreignNames.text: {T}：あなたの手札にある土地カードを１枚場に出してもよい。 この能力は、あなたがソーサリーをプレイできるときにのみプレイできる。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ
foreignNames.flavor: エルフ達ですらスカイシュラウドの森を真に知っているとは言えない。 レインジャーは単に、その不確かさを武器として扱うのに最も長けているだけだ。

foreignNames.name: Patrulheiro de Skyshroud
foreignNames.text: {T}: Você pode colocar um card de terreno em jogo vindo de sua mão. Use esta habilidade somente quando puder jogar um feitiço.
foreignNames.flavor: Nem mesmo os elfos conhecem completamente a Floresta de Skyshroud. Os patrulheiros são os mais preparados para lidar com sua incerteza.

foreignNames.name: Скайшраудский Лесничий
foreignNames.text: {T}: Вы можете положить карту земли из вашей руки в игру. Разыгрывайте эту способность только при возможности разыгрывать волшебство.
foreignNames.flavor: Даже эльфы по-настоящему не знают Скайшраудский лес. Их лесничие просто лучше вооружены для встречи с неизвестным.

foreignNames.name: 天帷流浪汉
foreignNames.text: {T}：你可以从你手上将一张地牌放置进场。 你只可以于你能使用法术的时机下使用此异能。
foreignNames.flavor: 就连地精都算不上熟知天帷森林。 护林兵只是其中最有能力对应未知状况者。

rulings.text: A spell or ability that counters spells can still target spells that can’t be countered. When that spell or ability resolves, the uncounterable spell won’t be countered, but any additional effects of the countering spell or ability will still happen.

Allosaurus Shepherd’s last ability overwrites all previous effects that set the affected creatures’ power and/or toughness to specific values. Other effects that set these characteristics to specific values that start to apply after the ability resolves will overwrite that part of the effect.

Effects that modify an affected creature’s power or toughness without setting it will apply no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change the creature’s power or toughness.
The affected creatures don’t lose any abilities when they become Dinosaurs.

rulings.text: Energy counters aren’t permanents. Paying {E} won’t satisfy a revolt ability.

Revolt abilities check only whether a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn or not. They don’t apply multiple times if more than one permanent you controlled left the battlefield. They don’t check whether the permanent that left the battlefield is still in the zone it moved to.

Revolt abilities don’t care why the permanent left the battlefield, who caused it to move, or where it moved to. They’re equally satisfied by an artifact you sacrificed to pay a cost, a creature you controlled that was destroyed by Murder, or an enchantment you returned to your hand with Leave in the Dust.
Tokens that leave the battlefield will satisfy a revolt ability.

rulings.text: A spell or ability that counters spells can still target spells that can’t be countered. When that spell or ability resolves, the uncounterable spell won’t be countered, but any additional effects of the countering spell or ability will still happen.

Allosaurus Shepherd’s last ability overwrites all previous effects that set the affected creatures’ power and/or toughness to specific values. Other effects that set these characteristics to specific values that start to apply after the ability resolves will overwrite that part of the effect.

Effects that modify an affected creature’s power or toughness without setting it will apply no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change the creature’s power or toughness.
The affected creatures don’t lose any abilities when they become Dinosaurs.

rulings.text: Energy counters aren’t permanents. Paying {E} won’t satisfy a revolt ability.

Revolt abilities check only whether a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn or not. They don’t apply multiple times if more than one permanent you controlled left the battlefield. They don’t check whether the permanent that left the battlefield is still in the zone it moved to.

Revolt abilities don’t care why the permanent left the battlefield, who caused it to move, or where it moved to. They’re equally satisfied by an artifact you sacrificed to pay a cost, a creature you controlled that was destroyed by Murder, or an enchantment you returned to your hand with Leave in the Dust.
Tokens that leave the battlefield will satisfy a revolt ability.

rulings.text: Energy counters aren’t permanents. Paying {E} won’t satisfy a revolt ability.

Revolt abilities check only whether a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn or not. They don’t apply multiple times if more than one permanent you controlled left the battlefield. They don’t check whether the permanent that left the battlefield is still in the zone it moved to.

Revolt abilities don’t care why the permanent left the battlefield, who caused it to move, or where it moved to. They’re equally satisfied by an artifact you sacrificed to pay a cost, a creature you controlled that was destroyed by Murder, or an enchantment you returned to your hand with Leave in the Dust.
Tokens that leave the battlefield will satisfy a revolt ability.

foreignNames.flavor: Noch nicht einmal die Elfen kennen den Wolkenwald genau. Ihre Waldläufer sind lediglich am besten dafür gerüstet, mit seinen vielen Geheimnissen umzugehen.

foreignNames.name: Explorador de Veloceleste
foreignNames.text: {T}: Puedes poner en juego una carta de tierra de tu mano. Juega esta habilidad sólo cuando puedas jugar un conjuro.
foreignNames.flavor: Ni siquiera los elfos conocen verdaderamente el bosque de Veloceleste. Los exploradores son simplemente los mejor equipados para manejar sus incertidumbres.

foreignNames.name: Ranger de Linciel
foreignNames.text: {T} : Vous pouvez mettre en jeu une carte de terrain de votre main. Ne jouez cette capacité que lorsque vous pourriez jouer un rituel.
foreignNames.flavor: Même les elfes ne connaissent pas vraiment la forêt de Linciel. Les rangers sont simplement les mieux équipés pour affronter ses mystères.

foreignNames.name: Ranger di Cielsudario
foreignNames.text: {T}: Puoi mettere in gioco una carta terra dalla tua mano. Gioca questa abilità solo quando potresti giocare una stregoneria.
foreignNames.flavor: Neppure gli elfi conoscono realmente la Foresta di Cielsudario. I ranger sono sì e no i meglio equipaggiati per affrontare la sua incertezza.

foreignNames.name: スカイシュラウドのレインジャー
foreignNames.text: {T}：あなたの手札にある土地カードを１枚場に出してもよい。 この能力は、あなたがソーサリーをプレイできるときにのみプレイできる。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ
foreignNames.flavor: エルフ達ですらスカイシュラウドの森を真に知っているとは言えない。 レインジャーは単に、その不確かさを武器として扱うのに最も長けているだけだ。

foreignNames.name: Patrulheiro de Skyshroud
foreignNames.text: {T}: Você pode colocar um card de terreno em jogo vindo de sua mão. Use esta habilidade somente quando puder jogar um feitiço.
foreignNames.flavor: Nem mesmo os elfos conhecem completamente a Floresta de Skyshroud. Os patrulheiros são os mais preparados para lidar com sua incerteza.

foreignNames.name: Скайшраудский Лесничий
foreignNames.text: {T}: Вы можете положить карту земли из вашей руки в игру. Разыгрывайте эту способность только при возможности разыгрывать волшебство.
foreignNames.flavor: Даже эльфы по-настоящему не знают Скайшраудский лес. Их лесничие просто лучше вооружены для встречи с неизвестным.

foreignNames.name: 天帷流浪汉
foreignNames.text: {T}：你可以从你手上将一张地牌放置进场。 你只可以于你能使用法术的时机下使用此异能。
foreignNames.flavor: 就连地精都算不上熟知天帷森林。 护林兵只是其中最有能力对应未知状况者。

cards.text:
This spell can't be countered.
Green spells you control can't be countered.

printings.name: Allosaurus Shepherd
printings.text:
This spell can't be countered.
Green spells you control can't be countered.
{4}{G}{G}: Until end of turn, each Elf creature you control has base power and toughness 5/5 and becomes a Dinosaur in addition to its other creature types.

rulings.text: A spell or ability that counters spells can still target spells that can’t be countered. When that spell or ability resolves, the uncounterable spell won’t be countered, but any additional effects of the countering spell or ability will still happen.

Allosaurus Shepherd’s last ability overwrites all previous effects that set the affected creatures’ power and/or toughness to specific values. Other effects that set these characteristics to specific values that start to apply after the ability resolves will overwrite that part of the effect.

Effects that modify an affected creature’s power or toughness without setting it will apply no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change the creature’s power or toughness.
The affected creatures don’t lose any abilities when they become Dinosaurs.

foreignNames.text: Wenn der Elfenpionier ins Spiel kommt, kannst du ein Standardland aus deiner Hand getappt ins Spiel bringen.
foreignNames.flavor: „Zerstörung ist das Werk eines halben Tages. Neuerschaffung ist ein Lebenswerk."

foreignNames.text: Cuando el Pionero élfico entre en juego, puedes poner en juego girada una carta de tierra básica de tu mano.
foreignNames.flavor: "La destrucción es la obra de una tarde. La creación es la obra de una vida".

foreignNames.text: Quand le Pionnier elfe arrive en jeu, vous pouvez mettre en jeu un terrain de base engagé depuis votre main.
foreignNames.flavor: « La destruction dure le temps d'un après-midi. La création dure le temps d'une vie. »

foreignNames.name: Pioniere Elfico
foreignNames.text: Quando il Pioniere Elfico entra in gioco, puoi mettere in gioco dalla tua mano una carta terra base TAPpata.
foreignNames.flavor: "La distruzione è il lavoro di un pomeriggio. La creazione è il lavoro di una vita".

foreignNames.text: Quando Pioneiro Élfico entra em jogo, você pode colocar em jogo, virado, um card de terreno básico de sua mão.
foreignNames.flavor: "Para destruir, gasta-se apenas uma tarde. Para criar, trabalha-se uma vida inteira."

printings.flavor: "The stories tell of a distant time when machines overran the forests, destroying everything that lived. That time will not come again."

foreignNames.name: Elfischer Raufbold
foreignNames.text: {G}, {T}, opfere den Elfischen Raufbold: Zerstöre ein Artefakt deiner Wahl.
foreignNames.flavor: „Die Geschichten spielen in einer vergangenen Zeit, als Maschinen die Wälder überrannten und alles zerstörten, was darin lebte. Diese Zeiten werden sich nicht wiederholen."

foreignNames.name: Elfo pendenciero
foreignNames.text: {G}, {T}, sacrificar el Elfo pendenciero: Destruye el artefacto objetivo.
foreignNames.flavor: "Cuentan de un tiempo distante cuando las máquinas invadían los bosques destruyendo todo lo que vivía. Ese tiempo no regresará".

foreignNames.name: Ferrailleur elfe
foreignNames.text: {G}, {T}, sacrifiez le Ferrailleur elfe : Détruisez l'artefact ciblé.
foreignNames.flavor: « Les légendes parlent d'un temps révolu où les machines dominaient les forêts, détruisant tout ce qui vivait. Je veillerai à ce que jamais ce temps ne revienne. »

foreignNames.name: Attaccabrighe Elfico
foreignNames.text: {G}, {T}, Sacrifica l'Attaccabrighe Elfico: Distruggi un artefatto bersaglio.
foreignNames.flavor: "Le leggende narrano di un tempo lontano in cui le macchine dominavano la foresta, distruggendo tutto ciò che l'abitava. Quel tempo non tornerà mai più".

foreignNames.name: Sucateiro Élfico
foreignNames.text: {G}, {T}, Sacrifique Sucateiro Élfico: Destrói o artefato alvo.
foreignNames.flavor: "As histórias falam de uma época distante em que as máquinas devastavam as florestas, destruindo tudo o que vivia. Aquela época não voltará."

printings.flavor: "I do not need to pierce your heart to still its beating."

rulings.text: Energy counters aren’t permanents. Paying {E} won’t satisfy a revolt ability.

Revolt abilities check only whether a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn or not. They don’t apply multiple times if more than one permanent you controlled left the battlefield. They don’t check whether the permanent that left the battlefield is still in the zone it moved to.

Revolt abilities don’t care why the permanent left the battlefield, who caused it to move, or where it moved to. They’re equally satisfied by an artifact you sacrificed to pay a cost, a creature you controlled that was destroyed by Murder, or an enchantment you returned to your hand with Leave in the Dust.
Tokens that leave the battlefield will satisfy a revolt ability.

{4}{G}{G}: Until end of turn, each Elf creature you control has base power and toughness 5/5 and becomes a Dinosaur in addition to its other creature types.

rulings.text: A spell or ability that counters spells can still target spells that can’t be countered. When that spell or ability resolves, the uncounterable spell won’t be countered, but any additional effects of the countering spell or ability will still happen.

Allosaurus Shepherd’s last ability overwrites all previous effects that set the affected creatures’ power and/or toughness to specific values. Other effects that set these characteristics to specific values that start to apply after the ability resolves will overwrite that part of the effect.

Effects that modify an affected creature’s power or toughness without setting it will apply no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change the creature’s power or toughness.
The affected creatures don’t lose any abilities when they become Dinosaurs.

printings.name: Arbor Elf
printings.text: {T}: Untap target Forest.
printings.flavor:
"I thank you once more, and I bid you farewell. May your forest grow again in peace."
—Aragorn

foreignNames.name: Lauben-Elf
foreignNames.text: {T}: Enttappe einen Wald deiner Wahl.
foreignNames.flavor:
„Ich danke euch erneut, und sage euch Lebewohl. Möge euer Wald wieder in Frieden wachsen."
—Aragorn

foreignNames.name: Elfo enramado
foreignNames.text: {T}: Endereza el Bosque objetivo.
foreignNames.flavor:
"Les doy las gracias una vez más y me despido. Ojalá su bosque crezca otra vez en paz".
—Aragorn

foreignNames.name: Elfe de la charmille
foreignNames.text: {T} : Dégagez une forêt ciblée.
foreignNames.flavor:
« Je vous remercie une fois encore, et je vous dis adieu. Que votre forêt prospère à nouveau en paix. »
—Aragorn

foreignNames.name: Elfo Arboreo
foreignNames.text: {T}: STAPpa una Foresta bersaglio.
foreignNames.flavor:
"Ora vi ringrazio di nuovo e vi dico addio. Possa la vostra foresta crescere in pace come prima."
—Aragorn

foreignNames.name: 東屋のエルフ
foreignNames.text: {T}：森１つを対象とする。それをアンタップする。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ・ドルイド
foreignNames.flavor:
「今一度お礼を申しあげる。そしてお別れを。願わくばあなた方の森が再び平穏に生い繁らんことを。」
——アラゴルン

foreignNames.name: Elfo do Arvoredo
foreignNames.text: {T}: Desvire a Floresta alvo.
foreignNames.flavor:
"Eu lhe agradeço mais uma vez e lhe digo adeus. Que sua floresta volte a crescer em paz."
— Aragorn

printings.originalText: {T}: Untap target Forest.

printings.name: Arbor Elf
printings.text: {T}: Untap target Forest.
printings.flavor: "The forest will surround you with its life if you are still and calm."

foreignNames.name: Lauben-Elf
foreignNames.text: {T}: Enttappe einen Wald deiner Wahl.
foreignNames.flavor: „Der Wald wird dich mit seinem Leben umgeben, wenn du still und ruhig bleibst."

foreignNames.name: Elfo enramado
foreignNames.text: {T}: Endereza el bosque objetivo.
foreignNames.flavor: "El bosque te rodeará con su vida si permaneces tranquilo y en calma."

foreignNames.name: Elfe de la charmille
foreignNames.text: {T} : Dégagez la forêt ciblée.
foreignNames.flavor: « La forêt vous réservera sa vie foisonnante si vous restez immobile et calme. »

foreignNames.name: Elfo Arboreo
foreignNames.text: {T}: STAPpa una Foresta bersaglio.
foreignNames.flavor: "Rimani immobile e mantieni la calma, e la foresta ti abbraccerà con la sua vita."

foreignNames.name: 東屋のエルフ
foreignNames.text: {T}：森１つを対象とし、それをアンタップする。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ・ドルイド
foreignNames.flavor: 「おとなしくしていれば、森はその生命でお前を包み込むだろう。」

foreignNames.name: 수목 엘프
foreignNames.text: {T}: 숲 한 개를 목표로 정한다. 그 숲을 언탭한다.
foreignNames.flavor: "가만히, 차분하게 기다리다 보면 어느덧 숲의 생명이 당신을 감쌀 것이다."

foreignNames.name: Elfo do Arvoredo
foreignNames.text: {T}: Desvire a Floresta alvo.
foreignNames.flavor: "A floresta o cercará com sua vida se você permanecer parado e tranquilo."

foreignNames.name: Эльф Лесного Свода
foreignNames.text: {T}: разверните целевой Лес.
foreignNames.flavor: «Если ты будешь сохранять неподвижность и спокойствие, лесная жизнь вскоре окружит тебя».

foreignNames.name: 乔木妖精
foreignNames.text: {T}：重置目标树林。
foreignNames.flavor: 「只要你保持冷静，树林将以其生命护你周全。」

foreignNames.name: 喬木妖精
foreignNames.text: {T}：重置目標樹林。
foreignNames.flavor: 「只要你保持冷靜，樹林將以其生命護你周全。」

printings.text: {T}: Untap target Forest.
printings.flavor: The Mul Daya elves reject their Tajuru kin, calling them arrogant tree-binders who think the roots serve the canopy.

foreignNames.name: Lauben-Elf
foreignNames.text: {T}: Enttappe einen Wald deiner Wahl.
foreignNames.flavor: Die Elfen von Mul Daya lehnen ihre Verwandten vom Tajuru-Stamm ab und nennen sie arrogante Bäume-Anbinder, die glauben, dass die Wurzeln dem Blätterdach dienen würden.

foreignNames.name: Elfo enramado
foreignNames.text: {T}: Endereza el bosque objetivo.
foreignNames.flavor: Los elfos Mul Daya rechazan a sus parientes Tajuru, llamándolos arrogantes arborícolas que creen que las raíces sirven a la enramada.

foreignNames.name: Elfe de la charmille
foreignNames.text: {T} : Dégagez la forêt ciblée.
foreignNames.flavor: Les elfes de Mul Daya rejettent toujours leurs cousins de Tajuru, les considérant comme des tordeurs d'arbre arrogants qui pensent que les racines servent la canopée.

foreignNames.name: Elfo Arboreo
foreignNames.text: {T}: STAPpa una Foresta bersaglio.
foreignNames.flavor: Gli elfi di Mul Daya hanno respinto da tempo la stirpe di Tajuru, considerata un ammasso di raccoglirami che non pensa ad altro che a rifugiarsi tra le radici.

foreignNames.name: 東屋のエルフ
foreignNames.text: {T}：森１つを対象とし、それをアンタップする。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ・ドルイド
foreignNames.flavor: ムル・ダヤのエルフはタジュールの一族を、梢に根が仕えていると考える尊大な樹の束縛者として拒絶している。

foreignNames.name: Elfo do Arvoredo
foreignNames.text: {T}: Desvire a Floresta alvo.
foreignNames.flavor: Os elfos de Mul Daya rejeitam seus semelhantes Tajuru, chamando-os de atadores de árvores arrogantes que acreditam que as raízes devem servir à copa.

foreignNames.name: Эльф Лесного Свода
foreignNames.text: {T}: разверните целевой Лес.
foreignNames.flavor: Эльфы Мул Дайя не признают своих родственников Таджуру, обзывая их заносчивыми древовязами, уверенными, что корни всегда служат кронам.

foreignNames.name: 乔木妖精
foreignNames.text: {T}：重置目标树林。
foreignNames.flavor: 这些认为根就是要用来服务林冠的特裘如亲戚，被讨厌他们的慕达雅妖精称为束缚树木的自大份子。

printings.name: Nettle Sentinel
printings.text:
Nettle Sentinel doesn't untap during your untap step.
Whenever you cast a green spell, you may untap Nettle Sentinel.
printings.flavor: Though Shadowmoor's monster-haunted wilds beckon, she never leaves her post.

rulings.text: Nettle Sentinel's triggered ability resolves before the spell that caused it to trigger. The ability will resolve even if that spell is countered.

foreignNames.name: イラクサの歩哨
foreignNames.text:
イラクサの歩哨は、あなたのアンタップ・ステップにアンタップしない。
あなたが緑の呪文を唱えるたび、あなたはイラクサの歩哨をアンタップしてもよい。

foreignNames.flavor: 怪物どもが跋扈するシャドウムーアの地がどれだけ誘おうとも、彼女は自分の持ち場を決して離れはしない。

foreignNames.name: 荨麻原哨兵
foreignNames.text:
荨麻原哨兵于你的重置步骤中不能重置。
每当你施放绿色咒语时，你可以重置荨麻原哨兵。
foreignNames.flavor: 暗影荒原充满怪物的原野虽诱人探险，她却从未离开岗位。

foreignNames.name: Nesselranken-Kriegerin
foreignNames.text:
Die Nesselranken-Kriegerin enttappt nicht während des Enttappsegments ihres Beherrschers.
Immer wenn du einen grünen Zauberspruch spielst, kannst du die Nesselranken-Kriegerin enttappen.
foreignNames.flavor: Obwohl die von Monstern heimgesuchte Wildnis des Schattenmoors sie lockt, verlässt sie nie ihren Posten.

foreignNames.name: Centinela de ortigas
foreignNames.text:
La Centinela de ortigas no se endereza durante el paso de enderezar de su controlador.
Siempre que juegues un hechizo verde, puedes enderezar la Centinela de ortigas.
foreignNames.flavor: Aunque los monstruos del Páramo Sombrío la atraen, nunca deja su puesto.

printings.name: Narnam Renegade
printings.text:
Deathtouch
Revolt — Narnam Renegade enters the battlefield with a +1/+1 counter on it if a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn.
printings.flavor: "I do not need to pierce your heart to still its beating."

rulings.text: Energy counters aren’t permanents. Paying {E} won’t satisfy a revolt ability.

Revolt abilities check only whether a permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn or not. They don’t apply multiple times if more than one permanent you controlled left the battlefield. They don’t check whether the permanent that left the battlefield is still in the zone it moved to.

Revolt abilities don’t care why the permanent left the battlefield, who caused it to move, or where it moved to. They’re equally satisfied by an artifact you sacrificed to pay a cost, a creature you controlled that was destroyed by Murder, or an enchantment you returned to your hand with Leave in the Dust.
Tokens that leave the battlefield will satisfy a revolt ability.

printings.originalText: {T}: Add {G}.

printings.name: Elvish Mystic
printings.text: {T}: Add {G}.
printings.flavor:
"The Three Rings of the Elves were not made as weapons of war or conquest—that is not their power. Those who made them did not desire strength or domination or hoarded wealth, but understanding, making, and healing, to preserve all things unstained."
—Elrond

foreignNames.name: Elfen-Mystiker
foreignNames.text: {T}: Erzeuge {G}.
foreignNames.flavor:
„Die drei Ringe der Elben wurden nicht als Waffen für Krieg und Eroberung geschmiedet — ihre Macht liegt anderswo. Jene, die sie fertigten, begehrten weder Stärke noch Herrschaft oder gehortete Reichtümer, sondern Wissen, Schöpfung und Heilung, um alles Makellose zu behüten."
—Elrond

foreignNames.name: Místico élfico
foreignNames.text: {T}: Agrega {G}.
foreignNames.flavor:
"Los Tres Anillos de los elfos no se crearon como armas de guerra o conquista. No es ese el poder que tienen. Quienes los forjaron no anhelaban ni fuerza ni dominio ni riqueza, sino comprender, crear y curar con tal de preservar todo de forma impoluta".
—Elrond

foreignNames.name: Mystique elfe
foreignNames.text: {T} : Ajoutez {G}.
foreignNames.flavor:
« Les trois Anneaux des Elfes ne furent pas créés comme des armes de guerre ou de conquête ; là n'est pas leur pouvoir. Ceux qui les ont forgés ne désiraient ni force, ni domination, ni richesse, mais la compréhension, la création et la guérison, pour préserver toutes choses immaculées. »
—Elrond

foreignNames.name: Elfo Mistico
foreignNames.text: {T}: Aggiungi {G}.
foreignNames.flavor:
"I Tre Anelli degli Elfi non furono fabbricati per servire come armi di guerra e di conquista: non è questo il loro potere. Coloro che li forgiarono non desideravano forza o dominazione, né accumulavano tesori; cercavano di capire, fabbricare e curare, per mantenere ogni cosa immacolata."
—Elrond

foreignNames.name: エルフの神秘家
foreignNames.text: {T}：{G}を加える。
foreignNames.type: クリーチャー — エルフ・ドルイド
foreignNames.flavor:
「エルフの三つの指輪は戦いや征服のための武器として作られたものではない――この指輪の力はそのようなものではない。三つの指輪を作った者たちは、力や支配や蓄えた富などは願わず、すべてを浄く保つため、理解し、作り、癒す力を望んだ。」
――エルロンド

foreignNames.name: Místico Élfico
foreignNames.text: {T}: Adicione {G}.
foreignNames.flavor:
"Os Três Anéis dos Elfos não foram feitos como armas de guerra nem de conquista — esse não é o poder deles. Os que os fizeram não desejavam força nem dominância nem acumular riquezas, mas entendimento, criação e cura, a preservação imaculada de todas as coisas."
— Elrond

items.name: Wildwood Tracker
items.text: Whenever Wildwood Tracker attacks or blocks, if you control another non-Human creature, Wildwood Tracker gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

printings.name: Wildwood Tracker
printings.text: Whenever Wildwood Tracker attacks or blocks, if you control another non-Human creature, Wildwood Tracker gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
printings.flavor: "This one was wearing shoes made of glass. She'll be no ordinary prey."

rulings.text: If you don't control another non-Human creature immediately after Wildwood Tracker attacks or blocks, its ability doesn't trigger at all. If you don't control one as the ability resolves, the ability does nothing. It doesn't matter whether you control a non-Human creature in between those times, or whether you still control one later in the turn.

foreignNames.flavor: „Die hier trug Schuhe aus Glas. Eine ungewöhnliche Beute."

foreignNames.flavor: "Esta llevaba zapatos de cristal. No será una presa común".

foreignNames.name: Traqueur de bois sauvage

foreignNames.flavor: « Celle-ci portait des souliers de verre. Ce ne sera pas une proie ordinaire. »

foreignNames.flavor: "Questa indossava scarpette di cristallo. Non sarà una preda qualunque."

foreignNames.flavor: "이 녀석은 풀을 엮어 만든 신발을 신고 있어. 평소 같은 사냥감은 아니로군."

foreignNames.flavor: "Essa aqui estava usando sapatos de cristal. Não vai ser uma presa comum."

foreignNames.flavor: «У этой на ногах стеклянные туфли. Необычная будет добыча».

items.name: Pelt Collector
items.text:
Whenever another creature you control enters the battlefield or dies, if that creature's power is greater than Pelt Collector's, put a +1/+1 counter on Pelt Collector.
As long as Pelt Collector has three or more +1/+1 counters on it, it has trample.

printings.name: Pelt Collector
printings.text:
Whenever another creature you control enters the battlefield or dies, if that creature's power is greater than Pelt Collector's, put a +1/+1 counter on Pelt Collector.
As long as Pelt Collector has three or more +1/+1 counters on it, it has trample.

rulings.text: As Pelt Collector’s first ability resolves, if the entering creature’s power is no longer greater than Pelt Collector’s power, or if Pelt Collector’s power has been raised to greater than or equal to the power of the creature that died, Pelt Collector doesn’t get a +1/+1 counter. Notably, this means that if Pelt Collector is still a 1/1 creature and two 2/2 creatures die, it only gets one +1/+1 counter as the first triggered ability resolves, and it will be too big to get a counter as the second triggered ability resolves.

If Pelt Collector is dealt lethal damage at the same time as a larger creature you control, they’re destroyed at the same time. Pelt Collector won’t get an additional +1/+1 from its ability in time to save it.

If Pelt Collector’s power becomes less than 0, a creature with 0 power (or with power less than 0 but still greater than Pelt Collector’s power) entering the battlefield or dying will cause its first ability to trigger.

If a creature with power less than or equal to Pelt Collector’s power enters the battlefield or dies, Pelt Collector’s first ability doesn’t trigger at all. You can’t try to raise that creature’s power or lower Pelt Collector’s to get a counter.

If the entering creature leaves the battlefield while Pelt Collector’s triggered ability is on the stack, use its power as it last existed on the battlefield to determine whether Pelt Collector gets a +1/+1 counter.
To determine if Pelt Collector’s first ability triggers when a creature dies, use its power as it last existed on the battlefield.

To determine if Pelt Collector’s first ability triggers when a creature enters the battlefield, use the creature’s power after applying any static abilities (such as that of Trostani Discordant) that modify its power.

rulings.text: The abilities a leveler grants to itself don’t overwrite any other abilities it may have. In particular, they don’t overwrite the creature’s level up ability; it always has that.

Effects that set a leveler’s power or toughness to a specific value, including the effects from a level symbol’s ability, apply in timestamp order. The timestamp of each level symbol’s ability is the same as the timestamp of the leveler itself, regardless of when the most recent level counter was put on it.

Effects that modify a leveler’s power or toughness, such as the effects of Giant Growth or Glorious Anthem, will apply to it no matter when they started to take effect. The same is true for counters that change the creature’s power or toughness (such as +1/+1 counters) and effects that switch its power and toughness.

If another creature becomes a copy of a leveler, all of the leveler’s printed abilities — including those represented by level symbols — are copied. The current characteristics of the leveler, and the number of level counters on it, are not. The abilities, power, and toughness of the copy will be determined based on how many level counters are on the copy.

A creature’s level is based on how many level counters it has on it, not how many times its level up ability has been activated or has resolved. If a leveler gets level counters due to some other effect (such as Clockspinning) or loses level counters for some reason (such as Vampire Hexmage), its level is changed accordingly.
If Joraga Treespeaker is level 5 or greater, it grants the mana ability to each Elf you control, including itself.
